record.title: Improving postoperative fluid pocket with an earlier positive surface swab
fairness: Observation with reassessment is the best offered plan. The resident must determine what compartment the positive culture actually sampled, then integrate the improving asymptomatic pocket and healed wound rather than treat the organism name in isolation.

Aspiration for a purported deep infection and cephalexin for a presumed current skin infection are credible errors. The sample location, absent communication and current wound findings resolve them. The statement that the pocket was not sampled is necessary specimen-provenance information, not a reason to remove a safety-critical distinction.

The explanation does not declare every surface swab meaningless, prove sterility or exclude future infection. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified and no unsupported aspiration deadline is taught.
The earlier swab and current improvement have clear chronology. This node stands alone, and its content does not require the separate later symptomatic-seroma case.

record.title: Reinforcement after a recognized and controlled enterotomy
fairness: Permanent macroporous synthetic reinforcement is a defensible best offered answer within the stated selected repair scope. The learner must distinguish a controlled bowel event with feasible closure from an unresolved emergency-abdomen problem, then resist automatically choosing a biologic implant because an enterotomy occurred.

The temporary-coverage alternative represents overreacting to the bowel event; biologic reinforcement is the closer material-selection error. The anatomical and physiological observations make these distinctions possible without a diagnosis label that names the implant.

Source control does not erase the occurrence of contamination. The explanation appropriately restricts its conclusion to the selected single-stage scope and does not recommend a universal emergency mesh plane. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

The exact newer guideline recommendation has not been independently verified in this offline review; this editorial PASS does not endorse its evidence mapping or confer clinical approval. Clinician sign-off should retain the conditional scope rather than turn this into a universal synthetic-mesh rule after any enterotomy.
The retrospective operative record is complete enough to stand alone and supplies the mechanism of the bowel injury, current bowel status, closure feasibility and decision stage.

record.title: Persistent focal pain after improvement with rehabilitation
fairness: The best offered answer is elective epigastric hernia assessment. The learner must distinguish the improved broad functional complaint from the persistent focal mechanical pain, then choose a different treatment pathway. This is moderate at the lower end, not a hard item.

The reduction response and painless broad ridge are necessary symptom-localization observations, not pre-answer diagnostic labels. Rehabilitation and observation represent attribution and symptom-significance errors; no option-length, grammatical, absolute or convergence shortcut independently selects the key.
The explanation appropriately recommends assessment rather than promising that an operation will relieve every symptom. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified from the supplied content.

The standalone presentation supplies the earlier rehabilitation and response; no missing preceding node is needed. Name, age, sex, short complaint and complete task are present. This is an offline editorial PASS, not source verification or clinical approval.

record.title: Recurrent deep mesh infection after drainage and directed therapy
fairness: The best offered answer is mesh excision with debridement. Collapsed cavity volume must be distinguished from eradication of a prosthetic infection; recurrent purulence, a tract to retained mesh and the same deep organism then justify changing source-control strategy despite stability.

The favorable mesh material/location and stable physiology make continued salvage a recognizable temptation. The update supplies the important counterevidence. Excision is not selected merely by being the longest or most cautious option, and the repeated retain-mesh component does not converge on the key.

The exact removal extent and reconstruction are appropriately left to the treating team. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the wording does not make a particular antibiotic duration or universal explantation threshold a rule.

The presentation and current update together establish the completed drainage and culture-directed course. The isolated node remains coherent without its former initial-salvage companion or that companion's feedback.

record.title: Broad functional symptoms with a separate reducible navel defect
fairness: Initial rehabilitation with observation of the focal defect is the best offered sequence. The resident must distinguish intact broad midline separation from the real focal hernia, attribute the complaint using the different symptom responses, and choose an initial treatment rather than operate on the most visible defect.

The absence of prior rehabilitation establishes treatment stage. All three options contain rehabilitation, so that word does not uniquely identify the key. The symptom responses are necessary localization evidence; removing them would make focal repair more defensible.

Immediate focal repair targets the wrong demonstrated symptom source; immediate plication escalates before a conservative trial. The explanation says rehabilitation can be considered and does not promise efficacy or turn examination support into a validated diagnostic test. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The node stands alone with no dependence on a later symptomatic-hernia case. Patient identity, demographics, complaint and task are complete.

case.presentation: Luis Carter, a 54-year-old man, returns to clinic after core rehabilitation for a broad midline ridge. His balance has improved, but lifting still produces focal pain above the navel. Standing examination shows fat protruding through a small gap there; pressure returning the fat through the gap stops the pain. The broad ridge itself is painless.

case.presentation: Daniel Brooks, a 58-year-old man, attends clinic while the founder reviews his hospital records after his first incisional mesh repair. Drainage had begun recently. At the recorded assessment he was alert, eating and haemodynamically stable. The operative record placed macroporous monofilament polypropylene outside the peritoneal cavity. CT showed a localized fluid cavity around part of that mesh. A deep sample grew bacteria; the skin opening communicated with the cavity. No bowel communication was demonstrated on the completed evaluation.
sourceLabels: SAGES laparoscopic ventral hernia repair guideline
Mesh infection outcomes after abdominal-wall reconstruction, tertiary-center cohort

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The drain reached the cavity, the antibiotic course matched the deep culture, and repeat imaging showed that the fluid cavity had collapsed. Purulent drainage nevertheless returned through a tract to the retained mesh. Repeat deep culture grew the same organism. Daniel remained stable.
decisionNodes.stem: Which source-control recommendation now best fits Daniel Brooks's persistent infection?

answerChoices.label: Excise mesh and debride the repair plane
answerChoices.rationale: Persistent microbiologically supported infection after adequate drainage and directed therapy raises a retained-prosthesis source-control problem.

answerChoices.label: Retain mesh and repeat drainage with directed antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: The cavity was already drained and the regimen matched the organism, yet infection recurred at the implant.

answerChoices.label: Retain mesh and excise the cutaneous sinus tract
answerChoices.rationale: Closing or removing the tract alone leaves the documented deep infected focus.

case.presentation: Maya Bennett, a 47-year-old woman, attends clinic because her middle abdomen domes and feels weak when she rises from a chair. Ultrasound during the movement shows the rectus muscles separating across a broad segment while tissue remains continuous between them. A separate small opening at the navel admits fat during straining and empties when she lies down. Pressing the navel and reducing that protrusion do not reproduce or relieve the weakness; supporting the broad midline does. She has not tried supervised rehabilitation.
sourceLabels: EHS rectus diastasis guideline
EHS/AHS umbilical and epigastric hernia guideline
EHS midline incisional hernia guideline
SAGES laparoscopic ventral hernia repair guideline
EHS/AHS rare-location and special-circumstance ventral hernia guideline

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial treatment sequence best fits Maya Bennett's abdominal-wall findings and functional complaint?

answerChoices.label: Start core rehabilitation; observe the focal navel defect at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: The broad intact midline and symptom response localize the functional problem away from the painless focal opening. Rehabilitation can be considered first while the reducible asymptomatic focal defect is observed.

answerChoices.label: Repair the focal navel defect; then start core rehabilitation at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Repairing the focal opening first targets a finding whose manipulation does not reproduce or relieve the complaint. It is not the supported initial treatment for this broad functional symptom.

answerChoices.label: Plicate the broad midline; then start core rehabilitation at follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Plication may be discussed for selected persistent functional symptoms, but no conservative treatment has been tried and the intact broad midline is not an acute defect requiring reconstruction.

decisionNodes.explanation: There are two findings: a broad intact but separated midline and a focal reducible opening. The weakness follows the broad segment, not the focal protrusion. Consider rehabilitation first and observe the asymptomatic focal defect. If symptoms instead localized to that opening and improved with reduction, the focal repair pathway would become more appropriate.

record.title: Broad functional symptoms with a separate reducible navel defect
fairness: Initial rehabilitation with observation of the focal defect is the best offered sequence. The resident must distinguish intact broad midline separation from the real focal hernia, attribute the complaint using the different symptom responses, and choose an initial treatment rather than operate on the most visible defect.

The absence of prior rehabilitation establishes treatment stage. All three options contain rehabilitation, so that word does not uniquely identify the key. The symptom responses are necessary localization evidence; removing them would make focal repair more defensible.

Immediate focal repair targets the wrong demonstrated symptom source; immediate plication escalates before a conservative trial. The explanation says rehabilitation can be considered and does not promise efficacy or turn examination support into a validated diagnostic test. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The node stands alone with no dependence on a later symptomatic-hernia case. Patient identity, demographics, complaint and task are complete.

case.presentation: Thomas Avery, a 60-year-old man, attends clinic after discharge while the founder reviews an outside emergency ventral-hernia operation. The trapped bowel regained perfusion after release. During adhesiolysis a full-thickness small-bowel enterotomy was recognized immediately and securely repaired. A limited local spill was removed; repeated inspection found no continuing leak, residual contamination or bowel segment needing reassessment. He was off vasoactive support before and after this event, with maintained perfusion and no ongoing resuscitation requirement. The fascia met with gentle approximation and a closed tissue layer separated bowel from the available reinforcement plane.
sourceLabels: EHS emergency primary ventral and incisional hernia guideline
WSES open-abdomen guideline
WSES complicated abdominal-wall hernia guideline, 2017

decisionNodes.stem: Which reinforcement strategy best fits Thomas Avery's recorded end-of-operation findings?

answerChoices.label: Complete repair with permanent macroporous synthetic reinforcement
answerChoices.rationale: The recognized repaired injury, source-controlled field, recovered bowel, stable physiology and directly closable wall fit the selected emergency repair scope. When mesh reinforcement is chosen in that scope, current guidance favors permanent macroporous synthetic material.

answerChoices.label: Complete repair with non-cross-linked porcine dermal reinforcement
answerChoices.rationale: A biologic material is not preferentially required by a controlled enterotomy in an otherwise eligible repair. Current guidance favors permanent macroporous synthetic mesh in this selected scope.

answerChoices.label: Defer reinforcement and use temporary abdominal coverage
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied observations establish direct closure feasibility and no remaining source-control, bowel reassessment or physiological indication for temporary coverage.

decisionNodes.explanation: The bowel event is explicitly a repaired enterotomy during adhesiolysis, not an unexplained opening. Interpret its control, the bowel and physiology, and direct closure feasibility before selecting reinforcement. These findings support the selected single-stage scope in which permanent macroporous synthetic mesh is favored. Continuing leakage, uncertain bowel or unresolved physiology would change the decision stage rather than automatically select a biologic implant. No emergency plane ranking is tested.

concept.displayName: controlled emergency material
concept.learningObjective: Infer controlled bowel-entry repair eligibility from operative findings, then select the appropriate reinforcement strategy rather than automatic biologic substitution or deferral.
concept.historyMigration: None. Existing meaning IDs and their entry stages remain exact. Four changed objectives receive new meaning IDs with prior identities recorded; no FSRS or frozen-save migration is authorized.

record.title: Reinforcement after a recognized and controlled enterotomy
fairness: Permanent macroporous synthetic reinforcement is a defensible best offered answer within the stated selected repair scope. The learner must distinguish a controlled bowel event with feasible closure from an unresolved emergency-abdomen problem, then resist automatically choosing a biologic implant because an enterotomy occurred.

The temporary-coverage alternative represents overreacting to the bowel event; biologic reinforcement is the closer material-selection error. The anatomical and physiological observations make these distinctions possible without a diagnosis label that names the implant.

Source control does not erase the occurrence of contamination. The explanation appropriately restricts its conclusion to the selected single-stage scope and does not recommend a universal emergency mesh plane. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

The exact newer guideline recommendation has not been independently verified in this offline review; this editorial PASS does not endorse its evidence mapping or confer clinical approval. Clinician sign-off should retain the conditional scope rather than turn this into a universal synthetic-mesh rule after any enterotomy.
The retrospective operative record is complete enough to stand alone and supplies the mechanism of the bowel injury, current bowel status, closure feasibility and decision stage.

case.presentation: Erin Walsh, a 56-year-old woman, attends clinic three weeks after laparoscopic ventral mesh repair. A painless soft fullness at the old sac is smaller than at the prior visit and does not limit movement. Ultrasound shows simple fluid, an intact repair and no tract to the skin. The incision is now closed without redness, tenderness or drainage; she has no fever. A result posted today reports methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus from a swab rubbed over a shallow skin separation at the earlier visit. The fluid pocket was never sampled.
sourceLabels: Mesh infection outcomes after abdominal-wall reconstruction, tertiary-center cohort
DailyMed cephalexin capsule prescribing information, October 2026
SAGES laparoscopic ventral hernia repair guideline

decisionNodes.stem: Which management plan best fits Erin Walsh's current fluid-pocket course and the newly posted culture result?

answerChoices.label: Continue observation with a clinic reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The shrinking painless simple pocket and healed noninflamed wound support observation. The earlier surface swab does not establish a deep organism in an unsampled pocket or a current clinical skin infection.

answerChoices.label: Perform sterile image-guided aspiration with culture
answerChoices.rationale: An improving asymptomatic pocket does not need aspiration merely to chase a surface-swab result. Puncture carries an inoculation concern; new symptoms or deep-infection evidence would change that balance.

answerChoices.label: Start oral cephalexin with a clinic reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: Cephalexin is a credible susceptible-staphylococcal skin-infection medicine, but there is no current inflamed wound or supported deep bacterial infection to treat. A positive prior surface swab is not itself an indication.

decisionNodes.explanation: Interpret the sample before acting on its organism: a prior surface swab did not sample this fluid. The current shrinking painless pocket and closed noninflamed wound favor observation. This does not prove that superficial swabs are always contamination or exclude future deep infection; new local/systemic findings would require reassessment. No antibiotic dose or aspiration deadline is implied.

question.explanation: Interpret the sample before acting on its organism: a prior surface swab did not sample this fluid. The current shrinking painless pocket and closed noninflamed wound favor observation. This does not prove that superficial swabs are always contamination or exclude future deep infection; new local/systemic findings would require reassessment. No antibiotic dose or aspiration deadline is implied.

concept.displayName: asymptomatic seroma observation
concept.learningObjective: Distinguish a superficial wound culture from an unsampled resolving postoperative pocket before selecting observation, aspiration or antibiotic treatment.
concept.historyMigration: None. Existing meaning IDs and their entry stages remain exact. Four changed objectives receive new meaning IDs with prior identities recorded; no FSRS or frozen-save migration is authorized.

record.title: Improving postoperative fluid pocket with an earlier positive surface swab
fairness: Observation with reassessment is the best offered plan. The resident must determine what compartment the positive culture actually sampled, then integrate the improving asymptomatic pocket and healed wound rather than treat the organism name in isolation.

Aspiration for a purported deep infection and cephalexin for a presumed current skin infection are credible errors. The sample location, absent communication and current wound findings resolve them. The statement that the pocket was not sampled is necessary specimen-provenance information, not a reason to remove a safety-critical distinction.

The explanation does not declare every surface swab meaningless, prove sterility or exclude future infection. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified and no unsupported aspiration deadline is taught.
The earlier swab and current improvement have clear chronology. This node stands alone, and its content does not require the separate later symptomatic-seroma case.

record.title: Functional assessment before selecting a thyroid biopsy target
fairness: The left nodule's suspicious morphology creates a credible competing impulse to biopsy immediately. The learner must interpret the suppressed TSH and elevated free T4, then sequence functional mapping before sampling.
Scintigraphy is the best offered next study. The history removes major uptake-confounding exposures without explicitly announcing the diagnosis. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The explanation prepares the functional question in N02 but does not give its exact sampling plan or the subsequent scan result; N01 remains self-contained.

record.title: Biopsy targeting after a scan identifies unilateral autonomy
fairness: The learner must correlate functional and structural findings, then spare the scan-concordant functioning target while sampling the distinct suspicious nonfunctioning lesion. Right-only and both-nodule sampling represent credible errors.
Left-nodule FNA is the best offered plan. The explanation correctly uses 'usually' rather than treating functioning nodules as an absolute no-biopsy rule.

The update follows N01 coherently and supplies the scan findings needed even if this node is encountered directly with its shared presentation. Earlier feedback teaches why mapping matters but does not dictate the returned target. No material nonmedical cue identified.
suggestions: Tighten the final explanation: sampling both does assess the left lesion; the error is unnecessary sampling of the right target, not failure to assess or prioritize the left.

record.title: A fluid-only aspirate from a purely cystic lesion
fairness: Ultrasound observation is the best offered plan. The pre-aspiration images describe a purely cystic lesion, and the current residual cavity is asymptomatic. A Bethesda I label on its fluid does not automatically establish the same repeat-biopsy need as an inadequately sampled solid nodule.

The learner must interpret the relationship between original morphology and specimen contents, then decide whether the usual nondiagnostic-cytology pathway applies. Repeat FNA is a credible overapplication of that pathway; diagnostic lobectomy is premature. This tests a practical exception to a core rule rather than recognition of a supplied benign diagnosis.

The absence of a solid component and pressure symptoms is decision-critical, not gratuitous exclusion of distractors. The case gives the pre- and post-aspiration chronology and stands alone. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The broad observation label does not justify inventing a specific follow-up interval.

record.title: Suspicious morphology after one adequate benign aspirate
fairness: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA is the defensible best answer at the supplied follow-up. Persistent suspicious morphology is documented, the one benign specimen was adequate and from the correct lesion, and there is no separate compressive or structural indication making lobectomy the preferred immediate step.

The consequential work is to reconcile suspicious imaging with genuine benign cytology, then choose repeat sampling rather than either reassurance or immediate surgical diagnosis. The record distinguishes this from an incorrect-target specimen and from repeated concordant benign samples. These are common nodule-management errors.

The joint review is not a key-only action because review has already occurred in shared context; every choice is a subsequent plan. The explanation accurately limits the reassurance from one benign aspirate without claiming that benign cytology is useless. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The one-year chronology and unchanged punctate foci are explicit. The singleton supplies all necessary context and does not require a prior-node result.

record.title: Autonomous nodule with persistent mechanical symptoms
fairness: Right thyroid lobectomy is the strongest offered treatment. Progressive dysphagia despite normalized free hormones and documented right-sided esophageal compression make a structural problem consequential; the contralateral lesion has undergone two adequate target-confirmed benign samplings.

The resident must distinguish successful biochemical control from unresolved mechanical disease, then choose treatment extent using the contralateral evidence. Iodine-131 remains a real treatment for autonomy, while total thyroidectomy is a plausible overextension in a patient with bilateral nodules. Both alternatives are materially less favored by the supplied record, not inherently invalid treatments in all patients.

The preference for definitive treatment does not uniquely select lobectomy because all three options propose definitive treatment. The contralateral workup is necessary to the extent decision. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the explanation appropriately says surgery is the stronger offered choice rather than asserting that radioiodine can never reduce compressive symptoms.
The standalone presentation includes function, structural imaging and prior tissue results. No former companion node is needed to establish either lesion's workup.

record.title: Symptom treatment when thyrotoxicosis reflects hormone release
fairness: The resident must interpret low uptake with the painless course and relevant exposure history as destructive hormone release, then choose symptom relief rather than synthesis blockade or anti-inflammatory treatment.
Propranolol is the best offered initial medication for this stable symptomatic presentation. Methimazole and prednisone represent plausible mechanism and painful-thyroiditis confusions.
No diagnosis is supplied before the decision, and the short medication labels are parallel. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; no unsupported numerical threshold is needed.

record.title: Residual T3 excess before nonurgent thyroidectomy
fairness: Further methimazole titration with deferral of the nonurgent operation is the best offered plan. T3 remains elevated despite a normal free T4 and controlled resting pulse; the suppressed TSH is not the finding that establishes residual hormone excess here.

Two consequential decisions survive the option set: identify the persisting disease-directed treatment need instead of escalating symptom blockade, then apply incomplete biochemical control to elective operative timing. The balanced four-choice matrix prevents a majority-component or uniquely comprehensive-key shortcut.

Stable dysphagia and absence of an acute airway problem are needed to distinguish elective preparation from an urgent exception. The explanation does not invent a dose or a treatment interval. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; it should not be generalized to prohibit every operation before biochemical normalization in every circumstance.
The singleton gives the known diagnosis, current drugs, response and operative urgency. No earlier treatment-response question is needed.

record.title: Central-neck management for small bilateral node-negative papillary cancers
fairness: The resident must separate the bilateral intrathyroidal primary burden from the indication for nodal surgery. Bilateral cancers can tempt bilateral clearance, but the small noninvasive cN0 profile supports avoiding routine prophylactic central dissection.

Observation is the best offered central-neck plan. The explanation properly qualifies the recommendation as not routinely requiring prophylactic dissection, rather than claiming that normal imaging excludes microscopic metastases.
The three choices concern the same nodal decision. The later postoperative surveillance event in N14 follows coherently, and this explanation does not give its marker-interpretation answer.

record.title: Rising antibodies despite unquantifiable thyroglobulin
fairness: Chest CT is the strongest offered next study. The sustained later anti-thyroglobulin antibody rise prevents treating unquantifiable immunometric thyroglobulin as reassuring; an adequate current neck survey does not explain that trajectory. The absence of prior radioiodine matters when ranking routine radioiodine surveillance scanning.

The learner must interpret the assay limitation and serial trend, then select a study beyond the already assessed neck while considering the treatment history. The same-assay specification and postoperative chronology earn their place. This is a challenging application of high-yield thyroid-cancer surveillance principles.

Repeating an already complete cervical ultrasound is a weak distractor, but it does not expose a unique answer without medical knowledge: both chest CT and a radioiodine whole-body scan are new studies. The remaining distinction requires clinical interpretation, so there is no decisive novelty-only cue.

No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The antibody rise is a reason to investigate, not proof of recurrence or lung metastases. Current guideline details governing imaging sequence were not independently reverified under the no-network constraint; this editorial PASS is not clinical sign-off or a universal imaging algorithm.

The exhibit supplies readable dates, units, assay type and all serial values. The singleton provides surgical and radioiodine history and the current structural assessment without relying on an earlier node.

record.title: Compartment surgery after an inaccurately labeled prior neck operation

cues.phrase: right level-IIa and level-IV nodal lesions
cues.why: The literal level labels allow exclusion of 'Right IV/Vb compartment dissection' by simple coverage matching. This weakens one foil but does not select the key: 'Excision of the sampled right nodes' also covers both documented targets. The compartment-versus-targeted-removal decision still requires medical reasoning.

fairness: Right IIa/III/IV/Vb compartment dissection is the best offered operation for the supplied resectable multilevel disease after prior removal of a single node. The lower-neck field omits proven IIa disease, while another isolated-node excision repeats the limitation of the earlier procedure.

The learner must reconcile the referral's 'neck dissection' label with what the operative and pathology records actually establish, then choose a compartment-oriented operation. That interpretation matters when distinguishing an inadequately treated compartment from recurrence after a genuinely comprehensive prior dissection.

The level names are decision-critical and should not be hidden to avoid the partial cue. Exact operative extent still requires specialist clinical review, particularly in reoperative anatomy; the explanation appropriately limits the principle to feasibility. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified, and the item should not be generalized to mandate reoperation for every small persistent node.
The singleton gives prior thyroid surgery, the actual prior nodal procedure, current mapping, tissue confirmation and resectability findings. No earlier nodal-workup question is needed.
suggestions: For a future harder variant, use a clinically credible competing field or reoperative strategy that also addresses all known involved levels; do not simply obscure the level labels. The current key remains defensible despite the one weak foil.

record.title: Incidental medullary carcinoma after unilateral thyroid surgery
fairness: Calcitonin/CEA and neck-ultrasound surveillance is the defensible best offered plan in the supplied incidental post-lobectomy setting: the tumor was completely excised, no pathogenic germline RET variant is reported, postoperative calcitonin is unquantifiable and imaging shows no residual disease. Automatic application of the initial untreated-MTC operation rule is the central competing error.

The resident must first distinguish an incidental postoperative diagnosis from initial surgical planning, then integrate hereditary, biochemical and structural evidence to decide whether completion is indicated. The two completion options are credible surgery-resident misconceptions. The longer surveillance label names a concrete follow-up plan rather than a generic 'individualized management' escape.

The RET, calcitonin and imaging negatives are decision-critical and should remain visible. A known medullary diagnosis is appropriate for this management task; it does not answer the postoperative extent question. This is a challenging exception within a high-yield cancer-surgery topic.

No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The exact incidental-MTC completion recommendation and its application still require Melissa's clinical sign-off; this no-network review does not claim fresh guideline verification. Surveillance here is not a declaration of cure or a rule that completion can never become appropriate.
The three-month postoperative chronology, germline result, biochemical values and residual-lobe imaging make the case self-contained. It does not require N17 or any earlier thyroid-lineage question.

record.title: Obtaining representative tissue from a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass
fairness: The resident must recognize an aggressive unresolved lineage problem, then choose tissue acquisition that can support architecture and ancillary studies before committing to resection. This contrasts meaningfully with the routine first-inadequate-nodule pathway in N03.

Image-guided core biopsy is the best offered plan in this context. An optimized repeat aspirate with appropriate ancillary testing can be useful in selected cases, so the explanation correctly avoids claiming that FNA can never diagnose lymphoma.

The stable airway findings permit diagnostic workup and are decision-critical rather than disposable reassurance. Autoimmune hypothyroidism is a legitimate clinical clue, not a language-only label giveaway. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
suggestions: Consider specifying representative viable tissue and appropriate ancillary specimen handling in post-answer feedback after clinician/source verification. Do not imply that any core containing only necrosis will settle the diagnosis.

record.title: A benign aspirate from a different thyroid target
fairness: The defensible best answer is ultrasound-guided right-nodule FNA. The specimen and needle records establish that the benign result concerns the left lesion; the separate right lesion has measured suspicious morphology and sufficient size to support sampling. Neither whole-gland reassurance nor immediate diagnostic lobectomy follows from these findings.

Two consequential interpretations remain: limit the benign result to its actual target, then apply the right lesion's risk features to choose initial tissue assessment. The side labels are necessary provenance, not a key-only wording match; every option concerns the right lesion. This is moderate application of core nodule assessment, not a hard item merely because two nodules are described.
The standalone case supplies the patient's age, sex, short complaint, prior sampling and current findings. No earlier node or explanation is required. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

record.title: Selecting the biopsy target in a multinodular thyroid
fairness: The learner must rank morphology against size, then select the target. The larger spongiform lesion is a credible size-driven error; observation of both misses the smaller suspicious lesion.

Left-nodule FNA is the best offered plan. A large spongiform nodule can sometimes also be sampled, so the explanation appropriately says it can be observed rather than asserting that sampling it is forbidden. The right-only option leaves the higher-priority lesion unsampled.
No material nonmedical wording shortcut or confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the named patient, age/sex and complete task are coherent.

record.title: Cross-sectional mapping when invasive thyroid cancer is suspected
fairness: Neck and mediastinal CT with IV contrast is the defensible best offered study. Retroclavicular nodal disease, the posterior interface, dysphagia and ipsilateral fold immobility establish a reason for cross-sectional operative mapping beyond the completed ultrasound.

The resident must infer possible deep/invasive disease and then weigh useful contrast-enhanced anatomy against a possible later radioiodine course. Noncontrast CT is a credible iodine-avoidance error; the two CT labels are parallel. Mentioning radioiodine introduces a real competing consideration rather than announcing that contrast is permissible.

The known papillary diagnosis appropriately precedes a different management task. Renal function and the absence of an acute airway problem support the proposed elective assessment. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; this review does not establish a particular postcontrast radioiodine interval.
This is a complete standalone case. It does not require the earlier mapping or later nodal-surgery task to supply the cancer diagnosis, imaging findings or current decision.

record.title: Methimazole adjustment with low free hormones and persistent TSH suppression
fairness: The table creates a genuine conflict: the learner must interpret low free hormones despite suppressed TSH, then reduce synthesis inhibition rather than maintain or increase it. The numerical choices are parallel and do not reveal the key without interpreting the data.

Reducing to 10 mg is the best of the three offered prescriptions. These observations establish dose reduction more securely than they uniquely establish an exact optimal dose; offline review does not independently verify that exact dosing choice. Melissa's exact-version dose review remains necessary.
The later fever/sore-throat event in N11 is a distinct, coherent complication rather than a restatement of this dose-adjustment lesson.
suggestions: Consider trimming the already-managed propranolol narrative. Keep the free-hormone/TSH discordance and explicit dose history, and have the named clinician verify the exact prescription.

concept.learningObjective: Use thyroid-hormone and clinical trajectories rather than persistent TSH suppression to adjust antithyroid and symptom-control medicines.

record.title: Methimazole adjustment with low free hormones and persistent TSH suppression
fairness: The table creates a genuine conflict: the learner must interpret low free hormones despite suppressed TSH, then reduce synthesis inhibition rather than maintain or increase it. The numerical choices are parallel and do not reveal the key without interpreting the data.

Reducing to 10 mg is the best of the three offered prescriptions. These observations establish dose reduction more securely than they uniquely establish an exact optimal dose; offline review does not independently verify that exact dosing choice. Melissa's exact-version dose review remains necessary.
The later fever/sore-throat event in N11 is a distinct, coherent complication rather than a restatement of this dose-adjustment lesson.
suggestions: Consider trimming the already-managed propranolol narrative. Keep the free-hormone/TSH discordance and explicit dose history, and have the named clinician verify the exact prescription.

record.title: Biopsy targeting after a scan identifies unilateral autonomy
fairness: The learner must correlate functional and structural findings, then spare the scan-concordant functioning target while sampling the distinct suspicious nonfunctioning lesion. Right-only and both-nodule sampling represent credible errors.

suggestions: Tighten the final explanation: sampling both does assess the left lesion; the error is unnecessary sampling of the right target, not failure to assess or prioritize the left.

record.title: Symptom treatment when thyrotoxicosis reflects hormone release
fairness: The resident must interpret low uptake with the painless course and relevant exposure history as destructive hormone release, then choose symptom relief rather than synthesis blockade or anti-inflammatory treatment.
Propranolol is the best offered initial medication for this stable symptomatic presentation. Methimazole and prednisone represent plausible mechanism and painful-thyroiditis confusions.
No diagnosis is supplied before the decision, and the short medication labels are parallel. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; no unsupported numerical threshold is needed.

fairness: The resident must separate the bilateral intrathyroidal primary burden from the indication for nodal surgery. Bilateral cancers can tempt bilateral clearance, but the small noninvasive cN0 profile supports avoiding routine prophylactic central dissection.

concept.learningObjective: Choose tissue acquisition before resection for a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass with unresolved lineage.

record.title: Obtaining representative tissue from a rapidly enlarging thyroid mass
fairness: The resident must recognize an aggressive unresolved lineage problem, then choose tissue acquisition that can support architecture and ancillary studies before committing to resection. This contrasts meaningfully with the routine first-inadequate-nodule pathway in N03.

Image-guided core biopsy is the best offered plan in this context. An optimized repeat aspirate with appropriate ancillary testing can be useful in selected cases, so the explanation correctly avoids claiming that FNA can never diagnose lymphoma.

The stable airway findings permit diagnostic workup and are decision-critical rather than disposable reassurance. Autoimmune hypothyroidism is a legitimate clinical clue, not a language-only label giveaway. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
suggestions: Consider specifying representative viable tissue and appropriate ancillary specimen handling in post-answer feedback after clinician/source verification. Do not imply that any core containing only necrosis will settle the diagnosis.

concept.learningObjective: Select ultrasound-guided FNA after normal TSH and ultrasound findings meeting biopsy criteria in the scoped stable outpatient pathway.

record.title: A benign aspirate from a different thyroid target
fairness: The defensible best answer is ultrasound-guided right-nodule FNA. The specimen and needle records establish that the benign result concerns the left lesion; the separate right lesion has measured suspicious morphology and sufficient size to support sampling. Neither whole-gland reassurance nor immediate diagnostic lobectomy follows from these findings.

Two consequential interpretations remain: limit the benign result to its actual target, then apply the right lesion's risk features to choose initial tissue assessment. The side labels are necessary provenance, not a key-only wording match; every option concerns the right lesion. This is moderate application of core nodule assessment, not a hard item merely because two nodules are described.
The standalone case supplies the patient's age, sex, short complaint, prior sampling and current findings. No earlier node or explanation is required. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

concept.learningObjective: Choose an additional anatomic study for suspected deep or invasive differentiated thyroid cancer.

record.title: Cross-sectional mapping when invasive thyroid cancer is suspected
fairness: Neck and mediastinal CT with IV contrast is the defensible best offered study. Retroclavicular nodal disease, the posterior interface, dysphagia and ipsilateral fold immobility establish a reason for cross-sectional operative mapping beyond the completed ultrasound.

The resident must infer possible deep/invasive disease and then weigh useful contrast-enhanced anatomy against a possible later radioiodine course. Noncontrast CT is a credible iodine-avoidance error; the two CT labels are parallel. Mentioning radioiodine introduces a real competing consideration rather than announcing that contrast is permissible.

The known papillary diagnosis appropriately precedes a different management task. Renal function and the absence of an acute airway problem support the proposed elective assessment. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; this review does not establish a particular postcontrast radioiodine interval.
This is a complete standalone case. It does not require the earlier mapping or later nodal-surgery task to supply the cancer diagnosis, imaging findings or current decision.

concept.displayName: Choose follow-up after a nondiagnostic aspirate by interpreting cyst morphology rather than the category alone.
concept.learningObjective: Choose follow-up after a nondiagnostic aspirate by interpreting cyst morphology rather than the category alone.

record.title: A fluid-only aspirate from a purely cystic lesion
fairness: Ultrasound observation is the best offered plan. The pre-aspiration images describe a purely cystic lesion, and the current residual cavity is asymptomatic. A Bethesda I label on its fluid does not automatically establish the same repeat-biopsy need as an inadequately sampled solid nodule.

The learner must interpret the relationship between original morphology and specimen contents, then decide whether the usual nondiagnostic-cytology pathway applies. Repeat FNA is a credible overapplication of that pathway; diagnostic lobectomy is premature. This tests a practical exception to a core rule rather than recognition of a supplied benign diagnosis.

The absence of a solid component and pressure symptoms is decision-critical, not gratuitous exclusion of distractors. The case gives the pre- and post-aspiration chronology and stands alone. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The broad observation label does not justify inventing a specific follow-up interval.

record.title: Suspicious morphology after one adequate benign aspirate
fairness: Repeat ultrasound-guided FNA is the defensible best answer at the supplied follow-up. Persistent suspicious morphology is documented, the one benign specimen was adequate and from the correct lesion, and there is no separate compressive or structural indication making lobectomy the preferred immediate step.

The consequential work is to reconcile suspicious imaging with genuine benign cytology, then choose repeat sampling rather than either reassurance or immediate surgical diagnosis. The record distinguishes this from an incorrect-target specimen and from repeated concordant benign samples. These are common nodule-management errors.

The joint review is not a key-only action because review has already occurred in shared context; every choice is a subsequent plan. The explanation accurately limits the reassurance from one benign aspirate without claiming that benign cytology is useless. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.
The one-year chronology and unchanged punctate foci are explicit. The singleton supplies all necessary context and does not require a prior-node result.

record.title: Autonomous nodule with persistent mechanical symptoms
fairness: Right thyroid lobectomy is the strongest offered treatment. Progressive dysphagia despite normalized free hormones and documented right-sided esophageal compression make a structural problem consequential; the contralateral lesion has undergone two adequate target-confirmed benign samplings.

The resident must distinguish successful biochemical control from unresolved mechanical disease, then choose treatment extent using the contralateral evidence. Iodine-131 remains a real treatment for autonomy, while total thyroidectomy is a plausible overextension in a patient with bilateral nodules. Both alternatives are materially less favored by the supplied record, not inherently invalid treatments in all patients.

The preference for definitive treatment does not uniquely select lobectomy because all three options propose definitive treatment. The contralateral workup is necessary to the extent decision. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the explanation appropriately says surgery is the stronger offered choice rather than asserting that radioiodine can never reduce compressive symptoms.
The standalone presentation includes function, structural imaging and prior tissue results. No former companion node is needed to establish either lesion's workup.

record.title: Residual T3 excess before nonurgent thyroidectomy
fairness: Further methimazole titration with deferral of the nonurgent operation is the best offered plan. T3 remains elevated despite a normal free T4 and controlled resting pulse; the suppressed TSH is not the finding that establishes residual hormone excess here.

Two consequential decisions survive the option set: identify the persisting disease-directed treatment need instead of escalating symptom blockade, then apply incomplete biochemical control to elective operative timing. The balanced four-choice matrix prevents a majority-component or uniquely comprehensive-key shortcut.

Stable dysphagia and absence of an acute airway problem are needed to distinguish elective preparation from an urgent exception. The explanation does not invent a dose or a treatment interval. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; it should not be generalized to prohibit every operation before biochemical normalization in every circumstance.
The singleton gives the known diagnosis, current drugs, response and operative urgency. No earlier treatment-response question is needed.

decisionNodes.stem: Which surveillance study should be arranged next for {patientName}?

answerChoices.label: Chest CT
answerChoices.rationale: The persistent later antibody rise limits reassurance from unquantifiable immunometric thyroglobulin. With an adequate current negative neck study, cross-sectional assessment of a common distant site is supported.

answerChoices.label: Repeat cervical ultrasound

record.title: Rising antibodies despite unquantifiable thyroglobulin
fairness: Chest CT is the strongest offered next study. The sustained later anti-thyroglobulin antibody rise prevents treating unquantifiable immunometric thyroglobulin as reassuring; an adequate current neck survey does not explain that trajectory. The absence of prior radioiodine matters when ranking routine radioiodine surveillance scanning.

The learner must interpret the assay limitation and serial trend, then select a study beyond the already assessed neck while considering the treatment history. The same-assay specification and postoperative chronology earn their place. This is a challenging application of high-yield thyroid-cancer surveillance principles.

Repeating an already complete cervical ultrasound is a weak distractor, but it does not expose a unique answer without medical knowledge: both chest CT and a radioiodine whole-body scan are new studies. The remaining distinction requires clinical interpretation, so there is no decisive novelty-only cue.

No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The antibody rise is a reason to investigate, not proof of recurrence or lung metastases. Current guideline details governing imaging sequence were not independently reverified under the no-network constraint; this editorial PASS is not clinical sign-off or a universal imaging algorithm.

The exhibit supplies readable dates, units, assay type and all serial values. The singleton provides surgical and radioiodine history and the current structural assessment without relying on an earlier node.

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 58-year-old man, attends clinic after total thyroidectomy for papillary carcinoma and outside surgery described in the referral as a right neck dissection. The operative note describes removal of one palpable right level-IV node through a short incision; pathology lists that single node. Current ultrasound and contrast mapping show resectable right level-IIa and level-IV nodal lesions, each with FNA confirming papillary metastasis. The left lateral and central compartments show no abnormal nodes; there is no encasement of major vessels or aerodigestive structures.

record.title: Compartment surgery after an inaccurately labeled prior neck operation

cues.phrase: right level-IIa and level-IV nodal lesions
cues.why: The literal level labels allow exclusion of 'Right IV/Vb compartment dissection' by simple coverage matching. This weakens one foil but does not select the key: 'Excision of the sampled right nodes' also covers both documented targets. The compartment-versus-targeted-removal decision still requires medical reasoning.

fairness: Right IIa/III/IV/Vb compartment dissection is the best offered operation for the supplied resectable multilevel disease after prior removal of a single node. The lower-neck field omits proven IIa disease, while another isolated-node excision repeats the limitation of the earlier procedure.

The learner must reconcile the referral's 'neck dissection' label with what the operative and pathology records actually establish, then choose a compartment-oriented operation. That interpretation matters when distinguishing an inadequately treated compartment from recurrence after a genuinely comprehensive prior dissection.

The level names are decision-critical and should not be hidden to avoid the partial cue. Exact operative extent still requires specialist clinical review, particularly in reoperative anatomy; the explanation appropriately limits the principle to feasibility. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified, and the item should not be generalized to mandate reoperation for every small persistent node.
The singleton gives prior thyroid surgery, the actual prior nodal procedure, current mapping, tissue confirmation and resectability findings. No earlier nodal-workup question is needed.
suggestions: For a future harder variant, use a clinically credible competing field or reoperative strategy that also addresses all known involved levels; do not simply obscure the level labels. The current key remains defensible despite the one weak foil.

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 49-year-old woman, attends clinic three months after outside right lobectomy for an indeterminate nodule. Permanent sections unexpectedly show a completely excised 2.2-cm medullary carcinoma. Germline RET testing reports no pathogenic variant. Postoperative calcitonin is below quantification and CEA is within its laboratory interval; ultrasound shows normal left-lobe parenchyma and no residual thyroid-bed or cervical nodal lesion. Plasma free metanephrine and normetanephrine and albumin-adjusted calcium are within their laboratory intervals.

question.explanation: The incidental post-lobectomy pathway differs from an untreated preoperative MTC diagnosis. No RET mutation, elevated postoperative calcitonin or residual imaging target is supplied to indicate automatic completion; surveillance is the best offered plan, with individual clinical review. The routine initial total-thyroidectomy rule should not be applied automatically after this evaluated presumed sporadic unilateral surgery with reassuring postoperative findings. Adding central surgery does not supply a missing indication for completion in the absence of the specified biochemical, hereditary or structural concerns.

record.title: Incidental medullary carcinoma after unilateral thyroid surgery
fairness: Calcitonin/CEA and neck-ultrasound surveillance is the defensible best offered plan in the supplied incidental post-lobectomy setting: the tumor was completely excised, no pathogenic germline RET variant is reported, postoperative calcitonin is unquantifiable and imaging shows no residual disease. Automatic application of the initial untreated-MTC operation rule is the central competing error.

The resident must first distinguish an incidental postoperative diagnosis from initial surgical planning, then integrate hereditary, biochemical and structural evidence to decide whether completion is indicated. The two completion options are credible surgery-resident misconceptions. The longer surveillance label names a concrete follow-up plan rather than a generic 'individualized management' escape.

The RET, calcitonin and imaging negatives are decision-critical and should remain visible. A known medullary diagnosis is appropriate for this management task; it does not answer the postoperative extent question. This is a challenging exception within a high-yield cancer-surgery topic.

No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The exact incidental-MTC completion recommendation and its application still require Melissa's clinical sign-off; this no-network review does not claim fresh guideline verification. Surveillance here is not a declaration of cure or a rule that completion can never become appropriate.
The three-month postoperative chronology, germline result, biochemical values and residual-lobe imaging make the case self-contained. It does not require N17 or any earlier thyroid-lineage question.

record.title: Plan en-bloc resection while preserving uninvolved bladder
fairness: En-bloc sigmoid colectomy with partial cystectomy is the best offered plan, contingent on clear margins. The learner must preserve the adherent interface, then determine whether the described bladder anatomy requires partial or total removal.

The options independently test interface violation and excessive organ removal. Focal dome involvement, separate trigone/ureteric entries and a usable remaining reservoir are necessary to distinguish the two en-bloc operations.
The task's margin contingency protects fairness rather than providing the extent of resection. Adherence is not equated with histologically proven invasion in the explanation.
The retrospective clinic frame is coherent and standalone. En-bloc resection of an adherent colon cancer and extent appropriate to anatomy are high-yield.

record.title: Surveillance after an advanced adenoma
fairness: Three-year surveillance is the best offered answer. The resident must distinguish laboratory processing from the endoscopic resection method, then combine complete en-bloc removal with the lesion size to select the surveillance pathway.

The six-month choice credibly tests mistaken classification as large piecemeal removal. Complete preparation, complete excision, clear assessed margins and relevant history are supplied; the one-year alternative is not made correct by any stated feature.
All choices are comparable interval labels. No statement gives the advanced-adenoma category or interval before answering.
Standalone and high-yield; the date of a preceding companion is unnecessary. Exact guideline intervals remain subject to clinical sign-off and offline-source limitations.

record.title: Integrate baseline and first surveillance
fairness: Five-year surveillance is the best offered answer under the named USMSTF framework. Interpret the baseline 14-mm adenoma category, then modify the subsequent interval using the normal first surveillance examination.

The three-year option incorrectly carries the initial advanced-adenoma interval forward unchanged; the ten-year option erases the relevant prior adenoma history. Both are credible errors and neither is a lexical outlier.
Both examinations, their adequacy, the complete initial resection and relevant exclusions are supplied. This standalone node does not rely on a preceding surveillance question.
Serial surveillance planning is high-yield. Guideline timing is assessed from established knowledge offline, not newly verified current guidance.

record.title: Initial treatment of an asymptomatic metastatic primary
fairness: Systemic treatment planning with the primary in place is the best offered sequence. An adult scope failing to pass does not by itself establish clinically significant obstruction when a smaller scope passes, bowel function continues and CT shows no proximal dilation.

Interpret primary-related complication status first, then apply the documented noncurative metastatic setting to treatment sequence. Colectomy and diversion are concrete, credible responses to overcalling obstruction.

The absence of bleeding/transfusion need closes another reason to intervene locally. These facts are decision-critical and do not amount to an author-supplied 'asymptomatic' diagnosis in the visible text.
Standalone and high-yield. The explanation appropriately uses 'generally preferred' rather than prescribing systemic treatment regardless of future symptoms or individual goals.

record.title: Rectal removal for uncontrolled FAP burden
fairness: IPAA is the best offered plan: repeated failure to clear the dysplastic rectal field argues against retaining the rectum; preserved continence and an informed continuity goal then favor restorative reconstruction over an end ileostomy.

These are two independent, consequential choices about extent and reconstruction. The preference is decision-critical because end ileostomy is otherwise a legitimate operation, not an unfair permission statement.
Known FAP is appropriate for an operative-management task. The standalone story and task are complete; operative selection in FAP is high-yield.

record.title: Reconstruction when continence is poor
fairness: Proctocolectomy with end ileostomy is the best offered plan. Uncontrolled rectal dysplasia makes IRA inappropriate; persistent formed-stool leakage and a disrupted weak sphincter make a pouch reconstruction unattractive.
Stoma acceptance is an informed-treatment constraint, not a direct instruction to select the stoma option. The two operative decisions remain grounded in disease and function.
Standalone context is sufficient. Integrating oncologic extent with functional suitability is high-yield; no numerical continence threshold is invented.

record.title: Rectal-sparing FAP operation
fairness: IRA is the best offered fit for documented limited, completely cleared rectal disease plus the informed preference to avoid pelvic dissection and accept surveillance. IPAA remains a legitimate alternative in selected patients, not a categorically incorrect FAP treatment.

The learner must determine whether retaining the rectum is defensible before applying the preference; the preference cannot replace that disease-distribution judgment. Retaining it protects the single-best-answer comparison.
Standalone and high-yield. No invented numerical eligibility cutoff is needed. Exact patient selection and counseling remain for Melissa Rowland's clinical sign-off.

record.title: Complete favorable invasive-polyp excision
fairness: Surveillance is the best offered plan: an intact oriented specimen, shallow invasion, explicit lateral and deep clearance, favorable grade and absent adverse features support local treatment despite the presence of submucosal carcinoma.

The lateral-margin repair supplies a previously important adequacy boundary. Regional colectomy remains a plausible overreaction to invasion; scar excision incorrectly treats a resolved local-clearance problem.

Interpretation of whole-specimen adequacy followed by local-versus-regional management is consequential and high-yield. The negative findings are needed to justify the best answer rather than simply decorate it.
Standalone and self-contained. The exact numerical observations are patient data; this review does not derive a new universal cutoff or adjudicate a disputed close-margin zone.

record.title: Count adenomas by lesions rather than fragments
fairness: The seven-to-ten-year interval is the best offered answer under the named USMSTF framework: establish the lesion count from the procedure record before applying the nonadvanced-adenoma surveillance category.

Four fragments versus two removed lesions creates a consequential counting error with a different offered interval. Specimen pooling does not warrant upgrading the number of adenomas from two to four.
Completeness, preparation, lesion sizes and relevant history are supplied. Options are parallel intervals with no key-only qualifier or explanation.
Standalone and high-yield. The selected interval is consistent with established guidance recalled offline; current source verification and clinical approval were not performed.

record.title: Advanced resection before colectomy
fairness: Advanced-endoscopy completion planning is the best offered route. Prior cautery and tattoo beneath the residual lesion create an alternative explanation for nonlifting, so the lift result cannot independently establish invasive cancer.
The learner must interpret the procedural history and the limited histology before selecting further therapeutic expertise rather than committing to oncologic resection or another superficial biopsy.
The concrete referral wording now distinguishes endoscopic completion from operative planning. It does not assert that completion will be easy or that invasion has been excluded.
Standalone and high-yield; the original lesion, intervention, residual tissue and subsequent finding are all present.

record.title: Choose reconstruction after emergency sigmoid resection
fairness: Rectal-stump closure with end colostomy is the best offered reconstruction at the stated decision point. Persistent vasopressor requirement, fecal contamination and edematous bowel favor avoiding an anastomosis; proximal diversion does not eliminate anastomotic failure risk.

The current question separates the completed source-control resection from the remaining reconstruction decision. Viable ends and feasible fascial closure make the scope clear without requiring the learner to invent a damage-control/open-abdomen plan.

All options are concrete reconstructions with comparable specificity; there is no uniquely generic emergency-treatment answer. The two steps are assessment of present anastomotic risk and selection of the appropriate reconstruction.

The retrospective clinic frame is coherent and self-contained. This is high-yield emergency colorectal judgment, moderate rather than hard, and the explanation appropriately avoids a universal Hartmann rule.

record.title: Early surveillance after piecemeal EMR
fairness: Six-month surveillance is the best offered answer under the named framework. Four overlapping captures establish piecemeal removal despite the single container/aggregate; a free edge on one fragment cannot establish clearance of the entire perimeter.
The resident must resolve procedure versus pathology provenance before applying surveillance timing. The three-year choice credibly overweights the adenoma histology or apparent local clearance.

Adequate whole-colon examination is explicit and options are parallel. The endoscopic absence of a remnant is appropriately included as a competing observation, not as a guarantee of complete histologic clearance.
Standalone and high-yield. This is surveillance timing, not an authored runtime test-wait duration.

record.title: Complete abnormal stool screening
fairness: Repeat colonoscopy with improved preparation is the best offered next investigation. The resident must reject the negative summary as inadequate proximal evaluation, then determine that the original positive FIT has not been resolved by the later negative FIT or cecal intubation.

CT colonography is a plausible alternative completion method in other settings, but no inability or contraindication to repeat colonoscopy is supplied here; it is not the best offered route after inadequate preparation.

The recorded withdrawal observations are decision-critical, not an authored 'inadequate examination' conclusion. Preparation wording appears in both procedural alternatives, avoiding a unique literal match.
The chronological sequence stands alone and the investigation task is complete. This is a high-yield screening-completion problem.

record.title: Neoadjuvant sequence for locally advanced rectal cancer
fairness: TNT followed by reassessment is the best offered sequence. Extramural extension, fascia contact and suspicious nodes require staging interpretation before choosing preoperative rather than immediate surgical treatment.

Retained mismatch-repair proteins, the location below the reflection, negative distant staging and fitness appropriately bound the pathway. A known adenocarcinoma diagnosis is necessary context, not a diagnosis-answer cue.
Immediate TME is a credible sequencing mistake; transanal excision is a weaker distractor, but still tests failure to apply the local extent. This is moderate rather than hard.
Standalone and high-yield. This verdict does not independently verify an exact current TNT regimen or imply automatic surgery regardless of reassessment.

record.title: Select a rectal organ-preservation pathway
fairness: Oncologic resection with TME is the best offered plan for enlarging palpable mural disease with corresponding MRI abnormalities after treatment. Superficial negative biopsies do not establish clearance of that deeper focus.

The resident must resolve specimen scope and serial response trajectory, then decide between organ preservation, local excision and regional resection. Her preference remains a genuine competing consideration without overriding progressive findings.

The story is self-contained: treatment and serial assessments are included without reliance on a prior node. This high-yield response-assessment decision is harder than simple complete-response recognition.

Exact organ-preservation versus radical-resection boundaries remain a clinician-review issue. This offline review finds no equally defensible offered alternative under the stated progression, but does not establish a general rule for every persistent ulcer or equivocal MRI focus.

record.title: Complete favorable invasive-polyp excision
fairness: Surveillance is the defensible best offered plan: interpret stalk submucosal invasion separately from actual cut-edge involvement, then integrate intact retrieval, clear clearance and absence of adverse histology. Neither scar excision nor colectomy gains an indication from stalk invasion alone.
The raw histology does not name a favorable-risk category. The reassuring findings are needed to distinguish local clearance from regional risk, rather than serving as nonmedical wording matches.
Standalone presentation supplies age, sex, lesion site and completed treatment. No preceding answer or absent future result is required. Malignant-polyp management is high-yield.

Offline editorial judgment only: current external guidance and source support were not independently verified, as network access was excluded. PASS is not clinical approval; this and all other reviewed drafts remain needs_clinician_review.

record.title: Regional risk despite local clearance
fairness: Oncologic resection is the best offered plan for the fit patient with invasive carcinoma actually transected and an unreconstructable specimen. Distinguishing a favorable-looking scar from histologic clearance, then choosing regional rather than local treatment, supplies two consequential steps.

Negative findings in represented fragments do not establish favorable histology for the whole lesion. Full-thickness scar excision is a plausible but insufficient local solution in this stated setting; surveillance is less defensible.
Standalone context is adequate and the incomplete malignant-polyp specimen is a high-yield decision. No categorical rule for every narrowly clear margin is asserted.

record.title: Regional risk despite local clearance
fairness: Colectomy with regional lymphadenectomy is the best offered plan. Recognizing malignant glands within endothelial-lined channels establishes a concern separate from the locally negative edge; a flat scar and unremarkable nodal imaging do not resolve microscopic regional risk.

Scar excision represents a credible local-versus-regional error and surveillance overweights local clearance. Operative fitness makes the comparison fair. The channel description requires medical interpretation and is not a lexical answer match.
Standalone and complete; interpreting adverse malignant-polyp histology to set surgical extent is high-yield.

record.title: Regional risk despite local clearance
fairness: Colectomy with regional lymphadenectomy is the best offered plan. Recognizing malignant glands within endothelial-lined channels establishes a concern separate from the locally negative edge; a flat scar and unremarkable nodal imaging do not resolve microscopic regional risk.

Scar excision represents a credible local-versus-regional error and surveillance overweights local clearance. Operative fitness makes the comparison fair. The channel description requires medical interpretation and is not a lexical answer match.
Standalone and complete; interpreting adverse malignant-polyp histology to set surgical extent is high-yield.

record.title: Regional risk despite local clearance
fairness: Oncologic resection is the best offered plan for the fit patient with invasive carcinoma actually transected and an unreconstructable specimen. Distinguishing a favorable-looking scar from histologic clearance, then choosing regional rather than local treatment, supplies two consequential steps.

Negative findings in represented fragments do not establish favorable histology for the whole lesion. Full-thickness scar excision is a plausible but insufficient local solution in this stated setting; surveillance is less defensible.
Standalone context is adequate and the incomplete malignant-polyp specimen is a high-yield decision. No categorical rule for every narrowly clear margin is asserted.

record.title: Rectal removal for uncontrolled FAP burden
fairness: IPAA is the best offered plan: repeated failure to clear the dysplastic rectal field argues against retaining the rectum; preserved continence and an informed continuity goal then favor restorative reconstruction over an end ileostomy.

These are two independent, consequential choices about extent and reconstruction. The preference is decision-critical because end ileostomy is otherwise a legitimate operation, not an unfair permission statement.
Known FAP is appropriate for an operative-management task. The standalone story and task are complete; operative selection in FAP is high-yield.

fairness: IRA is the best offered fit for documented limited, completely cleared rectal disease plus the informed preference to avoid pelvic dissection and accept surveillance. IPAA remains a legitimate alternative in selected patients, not a categorically incorrect FAP treatment.

Standalone and high-yield. No invented numerical eligibility cutoff is needed. Exact patient selection and counseling remain for Melissa Rowland's clinical sign-off.

record.title: Reconstruction when continence is poor
fairness: Proctocolectomy with end ileostomy is the best offered plan. Uncontrolled rectal dysplasia makes IRA inappropriate; persistent formed-stool leakage and a disrupted weak sphincter make a pouch reconstruction unattractive.
Stoma acceptance is an informed-treatment constraint, not a direct instruction to select the stoma option. The two operative decisions remain grounded in disease and function.
Standalone context is sufficient. Integrating oncologic extent with functional suitability is high-yield; no numerical continence threshold is invented.

concept.learningObjective: Use local stage and threatened planes to select treatment before definitive surgery.

record.title: Neoadjuvant sequence for locally advanced rectal cancer
fairness: TNT followed by reassessment is the best offered sequence. Extramural extension, fascia contact and suspicious nodes require staging interpretation before choosing preoperative rather than immediate surgical treatment.

Retained mismatch-repair proteins, the location below the reflection, negative distant staging and fitness appropriately bound the pathway. A known adenocarcinoma diagnosis is necessary context, not a diagnosis-answer cue.
Immediate TME is a credible sequencing mistake; transanal excision is a weaker distractor, but still tests failure to apply the local extent. This is moderate rather than hard.
Standalone and high-yield. This verdict does not independently verify an exact current TNT regimen or imply automatic surgery regardless of reassessment.

record.title: Select a rectal organ-preservation pathway
fairness: Oncologic resection with TME is the best offered plan for enlarging palpable mural disease with corresponding MRI abnormalities after treatment. Superficial negative biopsies do not establish clearance of that deeper focus.

The resident must resolve specimen scope and serial response trajectory, then decide between organ preservation, local excision and regional resection. Her preference remains a genuine competing consideration without overriding progressive findings.

The story is self-contained: treatment and serial assessments are included without reliance on a prior node. This high-yield response-assessment decision is harder than simple complete-response recognition.

Exact organ-preservation versus radical-resection boundaries remain a clinician-review issue. This offline review finds no equally defensible offered alternative under the stated progression, but does not establish a general rule for every persistent ulcer or equivocal MRI focus.

record.title: Count adenomas by lesions rather than fragments
fairness: The seven-to-ten-year interval is the best offered answer under the named USMSTF framework: establish the lesion count from the procedure record before applying the nonadvanced-adenoma surveillance category.

Four fragments versus two removed lesions creates a consequential counting error with a different offered interval. Specimen pooling does not warrant upgrading the number of adenomas from two to four.
Completeness, preparation, lesion sizes and relevant history are supplied. Options are parallel intervals with no key-only qualifier or explanation.
Standalone and high-yield. The selected interval is consistent with established guidance recalled offline; current source verification and clinical approval were not performed.

record.title: Complete abnormal stool screening
fairness: Repeat colonoscopy with improved preparation is the best offered next investigation. The resident must reject the negative summary as inadequate proximal evaluation, then determine that the original positive FIT has not been resolved by the later negative FIT or cecal intubation.

CT colonography is a plausible alternative completion method in other settings, but no inability or contraindication to repeat colonoscopy is supplied here; it is not the best offered route after inadequate preparation.

The recorded withdrawal observations are decision-critical, not an authored 'inadequate examination' conclusion. Preparation wording appears in both procedural alternatives, avoiding a unique literal match.
The chronological sequence stands alone and the investigation task is complete. This is a high-yield screening-completion problem.

record.title: Surveillance after an advanced adenoma
fairness: Three-year surveillance is the best offered answer. The resident must distinguish laboratory processing from the endoscopic resection method, then combine complete en-bloc removal with the lesion size to select the surveillance pathway.

The six-month choice credibly tests mistaken classification as large piecemeal removal. Complete preparation, complete excision, clear assessed margins and relevant history are supplied; the one-year alternative is not made correct by any stated feature.
All choices are comparable interval labels. No statement gives the advanced-adenoma category or interval before answering.
Standalone and high-yield; the date of a preceding companion is unnecessary. Exact guideline intervals remain subject to clinical sign-off and offline-source limitations.
