record.title: Bleeding admission review
fairness: Continuing octreotide and ceftriaxone while stopping empirical pantoprazole is the best listed plan for the documented immediate post-endoscopy variceal phase without another acid-related indication. Stopping either acute vasoactive therapy or antibiotic prophylaxis just because banding achieved hemostasis is the credible competing error.
The three options balance components: each drug appears in two continue clauses and one stop clause. There is no majority-component convergence or uniquely comprehensive key.

Two steps remain: interpret the confirmed source and successful hemostasis without treating the acute episode as finished, then distinguish medicines to continue from empirical acid suppression that can be stopped. This is high-yield phase-specific management.

The case stands alone and states the medications, endoscopy findings and current phase. Post-banding acid suppression practices can vary; the explanation correctly frames its cited recommendation as conditional on no other indication, rather than forbidding all post-banding PPI use. Current guideline wording was not independently verified offline, and no confident clinical inaccuracy is asserted.

record.title: Biopsy result review
fairness: Elective resection is the defensible listed answer for the stated proven beta-catenin-activated adenoma; regression and small size do not negate the supplied molecular risk. Surveillance is a credible size/response-based error; no hemorrhagic indication for embolization is supplied.

The learner must weigh the discordant implications of regression and tissue risk, then choose management. This is a high-yield adenoma exception. Naming the established diagnosis is appropriate because the task is management, not diagnosis.

The record explicitly identifies an already obtained, same-target tissue result, so it neither requires an unseen prior part nor implies routine biopsy of every adenoma. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical cue identified. Molecular-subtype nuances are not independently source-verified in this offline review.

record.title: Liver lesion review
fairness: Elective resection planning is the single best listed plan for established hepatocellular adenoma in an operable man despite regression after steroid withdrawal. Surveillance is a credible regression/size-based error; embolization is less appropriate without hemorrhage or an operative barrier.

Two consequential judgments remain: distinguish response to withdrawal from removal of lesion-specific risk, then select definitive management using sex-specific risk. This is high-yield benign-liver management, not merely recognition of an adenoma.

The follow-up framing is self-contained: lesion identity, interval measurements, steroid cessation and operability are all provided. No earlier node is needed. No nonclinical cue or confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

record.title: Ascites cause review
fairness: The serum-ascites albumin gradient is correctly calculated as 3.6 minus 1.1 = 2.5 g/dL. The high fluid protein and persistently distended upright neck veins favor a cardiac contribution, making echocardiography the best listed next evaluation.

Venous Doppler is a credible competing investigation for portal/hepatic venous disease, but the neck-vein findings and protein-rich fluid favor cardiac evaluation first. A nodular liver image alone does not establish the new ascites mechanism.

The learner must interpret fluid physiology and integrate it with examination before selecting a study. This is a high-yield, moderate two-step item. It is standalone, the task is complete, and the explanation appropriately says the findings raise rather than prove a cardiac mechanism. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical cue identified.

record.title: Medication review

cues.phrase: and add no opioid
cues.why: A minor avoidable negative-plan qualifier in the acetaminophen distractor. It is not a decisive giveaway, but stating the proposed acetaminophen schedule is enough.

fairness: Retaining the conservative acetaminophen schedule and adding carefully monitored short-acting hydromorphone is the best listed adjustment for function-limiting acute postoperative pain with renal/fluid deterioration during NSAID exposure. Celecoxib does not remove the relevant systemic NSAID concern.

The arithmetic is correct: 500 mg every 6 hours totals 2 g/day, whereas 1 g every 6 hours totals 4 g/day. The explanation scopes 2 g to a conservative cirrhosis regimen, not a universal toxicologic threshold.

The learner integrates the existing regimen and treatment response with renal/fluid risk, then chooses escalation. This is a high-yield, moderate two-step medication decision. Alertness, respiratory status and ward reassessment are relevant safety context; oral intake does not uniquely identify the key because all plans are oral.

The recorded inpatient time is clear despite the clinic review frame. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Exact dosing and monitoring remain clinician decisions, not independently verified by this offline review.
suggestions: Optional wording cleanup: remove the negative add-no-opioid clause while keeping the actual competing schedule. Preserve the conservative-regimen qualification in feedback.

record.title: Fluid treatment review
fairness: Holding diuretics and giving isotonic volume expansion is the best listed response to marked weight loss, orthostatic symptoms/blood-pressure fall and rising creatinine after dose escalation with hyponatremia. Persistent ascites does not establish adequate circulating volume.

Continuing diuresis with water restriction is a credible hypervolemic-hyponatremia error; escalating diuresis/paracentesis mistakes residual peritoneal fluid for a reason to intensify depletion. The clinical course separates these from the key.

The learner identifies the volume mechanism from treatment response and examination, then chooses the fluid/diuretic direction. This is high-yield moderate reasoning. Alertness and absence of seizures appropriately bound the offered acute sodium strategies without inventing a correction rate.
All necessary timeline and observations are in this standalone case. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical cue identified.

record.title: Incidental mass review
fairness: The dynamic enhancement pattern, long stability and lack of attributable symptoms favor a typical hemangioma and routine care among the choices. Annual imaging is a credible size-driven error; enucleation is less appropriate without symptoms or another complication.

Two steps are required: recognize the lesion from raw enhancement observations, then decide whether its large size changes management in this stable asymptomatic setting. This is high-yield benign-liver reasoning.

The presentation and exhibit supply the necessary context in one case. The lesion diagnosis is not disclosed before answering, and option specificity is reasonably balanced. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; no new surveillance interval or size threshold is inferred.

record.title: Cyst admission review
fairness: The daughter-cyst morphology and membrane-containing communicating biliary process support complicated hepatic echinococcosis. Specialist surgery with antiparasitic planning after stabilization is the best listed definitive pathway; communicating biliary disease makes PAIR an important but inappropriate competing shortcut, and medication with observation inadequately addresses the stated complication.

Two consequential steps are required: infer the disease and recognize that the demonstrated duct communication changes cyst-directed management after initial biliary decompression. This is a high-yield surgical complication/contraindication concept; hard is a qualitative prediction based on applying a less routine procedural boundary, not on obscure wording.

All three choices describe cyst-directed treatment at the same phase. The task distinguishes definitive cyst care from the antimicrobial/biliary care already underway, so the record is coherent and standalone. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical cue identified.

The item does not supply enough anatomy to choose one exact cyst operation, and appropriately does not ask for one. Contemporary procedural guidance was not independently source-verified in this offline review.

record.title: Bleeding admission review
fairness: Pre-emptive covered TIPS is the best listed pathway for the stated Child-Pugh C11 patient in the early window after control of esophageal variceal bleeding. Serial banding plus nonselective beta blockade is a credible alternative for a different risk group; an elective distal splenorenal shunt is substantially less attractive in this decompensated setting.

The resident must recognize that initial hemostasis does not remove the high-risk indication and apply severity plus timing to choose early escalation. This is a high-yield, moderate two-step management decision. A documented Child-Pugh score is appropriate data because score reconstruction is not the task.

Although the presentation first describes a pre-endoscopy chart review, the current update clearly advances to the result and post-hemostasis assessment. The node contains all decision data and stands alone.

No nonclinical cue or confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The explanation appropriately describes TIPS assessment; it should not imply that the few listed workup findings replace complete candidacy evaluation. Contemporary eligibility guidance was not independently verified offline.

record.title: Abscess course review
fairness: Image-guided drainage is the best additional treatment for a persistently symptomatic enlarging liquefied liver cavity despite an active antibiotic, with a percutaneous route and no generalized peritonitis. Broadening antibiotics is a credible but insufficient source-control response; segmental resection is excessive without a supplied failure or anatomical indication.

The resident must distinguish antimicrobial susceptibility from effective source control, then choose the appropriate intervention based on cavity evolution and access. This is high-yield moderate reasoning. The access finding is decision-critical anatomy, not merely a sentence promising that the service is available.

The standalone case contains the initial infection record, treatment response and relevant imaging. It needs no absent companion or later drain-failure result. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical cue identified. The feedback appropriately avoids unsupported universal drainage-technique or size rules.

record.title: Recurrent bleeding review
fairness: TIPS is the best listed escalation pathway after recurrent esophageal variceal bleeding despite documented combined prevention. Switching beta blockers or increasing ligation frequency does not address the demonstrated failure as directly.

The two consequential judgments are to distinguish recurrence despite actual combined therapy from an adherence/omission problem, then select the next prevention strategy after acute control. This is high-yield and moderate; the required treatment history is clinical evidence, not an unfair giveaway.
The case is standalone, and the task clearly asks about prevention after the latest bleed is controlled. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical wording shortcut identified.

Tolerated nadolol does not quantify dose optimization, and the listed specialist findings are not an exhaustive TIPS assessment. These are limits of the vignette, not sufficient evidence that a different listed option is best. The explanation appropriately conditions the pathway on candidacy assessment; contemporary eligibility guidance was not independently verified offline.

fairness: The dynamic enhancement pattern, long stability and lack of attributable symptoms favor a typical hemangioma and routine care among the choices. Annual imaging is a credible size-driven error; enucleation is less appropriate without symptoms or another complication.

Two steps are required: recognize the lesion from raw enhancement observations, then decide whether its large size changes management in this stable asymptomatic setting. This is high-yield benign-liver reasoning.

The presentation and exhibit supply the necessary context in one case. The lesion diagnosis is not disclosed before answering, and option specificity is reasonably balanced. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; no new surveillance interval or size threshold is inferred.

answerChoices.label: Retain the acetaminophen schedule and add low-dose short-acting hydromorphone as needed
answerChoices.rationale: The schedule totals 2 g daily, already the conservative AASLD cirrhosis regimen. A carefully monitored short-acting opioid can address acute pain without restarting a systemic NSAID.

answerChoices.label: Increase acetaminophen to 1 g every 6 hours and add no opioid
answerChoices.rationale: This doubles the schedule to 4 g daily, above the conservative cirrhosis regimen used here. The comparison is not a universal toxicity threshold.

answerChoices.rationale: A systemic NSAID is unfavorable during kidney and fluid deterioration in cirrhosis, although it may appear to avoid opioid sedation.

concept.displayName: Choose an analgesic class during cirrhotic renal deterioration
concept.learningObjective: Integrate the changed renal/fluid course with the actual analgesic exposure and avoid a within-NSAID substitution.

record.title: Medication review

cues.phrase: and add no opioid
cues.why: A minor avoidable negative-plan qualifier in the acetaminophen distractor. It is not a decisive giveaway, but stating the proposed acetaminophen schedule is enough.

fairness: Retaining the conservative acetaminophen schedule and adding carefully monitored short-acting hydromorphone is the best listed adjustment for function-limiting acute postoperative pain with renal/fluid deterioration during NSAID exposure. Celecoxib does not remove the relevant systemic NSAID concern.

The arithmetic is correct: 500 mg every 6 hours totals 2 g/day, whereas 1 g every 6 hours totals 4 g/day. The explanation scopes 2 g to a conservative cirrhosis regimen, not a universal toxicologic threshold.

The learner integrates the existing regimen and treatment response with renal/fluid risk, then chooses escalation. This is a high-yield, moderate two-step medication decision. Alertness, respiratory status and ward reassessment are relevant safety context; oral intake does not uniquely identify the key because all plans are oral.

The recorded inpatient time is clear despite the clinic review frame. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. Exact dosing and monitoring remain clinician decisions, not independently verified by this offline review.
suggestions: Optional wording cleanup: remove the negative add-no-opioid clause while keeping the actual competing schedule. Preserve the conservative-regimen qualification in feedback.

decisionNodes.stem: Which investigation should be arranged next to evaluate the leading cause of {patientName}'s ascites?

answerChoices.label: Transthoracic echocardiography
answerChoices.rationale: The high gradient with protein-rich fluid and elevated venous pressure raises a cardiac cause.

answerChoices.label: Transjugular liver biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: The nodular-liver label tempts confirmation of cirrhosis, but it does not explain the complete fluid/venous pattern.

answerChoices.label: Portal and hepatic venous Doppler ultrasound
answerChoices.rationale: Venous obstruction is a real alternative, but the protein-rich high-gradient fluid and systemic venous findings make cardiac assessment the leading next inquiry.

decisionNodes.explanation: The albumin gradient is 2.5 g/dL and supports portal-hypertensive physiology. The high fluid protein and neck-vein findings raise a cardiac mechanism rather than proving cirrhosis is the sole explanation. Echocardiography should evaluate that possibility.

record.title: Ascites cause review
fairness: The serum-ascites albumin gradient is correctly calculated as 3.6 minus 1.1 = 2.5 g/dL. The high fluid protein and persistently distended upright neck veins favor a cardiac contribution, making echocardiography the best listed next evaluation.

concept.learningObjective: Distinguish intravascular volume depletion from excess total-body fluid when choosing a hyponatremia strategy.

record.title: Fluid treatment review
fairness: Holding diuretics and giving isotonic volume expansion is the best listed response to marked weight loss, orthostatic symptoms/blood-pressure fall and rising creatinine after dose escalation with hyponatremia. Persistent ascites does not establish adequate circulating volume.

Continuing diuresis with water restriction is a credible hypervolemic-hyponatremia error; escalating diuresis/paracentesis mistakes residual peritoneal fluid for a reason to intensify depletion. The clinical course separates these from the key.

The learner identifies the volume mechanism from treatment response and examination, then chooses the fluid/diuretic direction. This is high-yield moderate reasoning. Alertness and absence of seizures appropriately bound the offered acute sodium strategies without inventing a correction rate.
All necessary timeline and observations are in this standalone case. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical cue identified.

record.title: Bleeding admission review
fairness: Continuing octreotide and ceftriaxone while stopping empirical pantoprazole is the best listed plan for the documented immediate post-endoscopy variceal phase without another acid-related indication. Stopping either acute vasoactive therapy or antibiotic prophylaxis just because banding achieved hemostasis is the credible competing error.
The three options balance components: each drug appears in two continue clauses and one stop clause. There is no majority-component convergence or uniquely comprehensive key.

Two steps remain: interpret the confirmed source and successful hemostasis without treating the acute episode as finished, then distinguish medicines to continue from empirical acid suppression that can be stopped. This is high-yield phase-specific management.

The case stands alone and states the medications, endoscopy findings and current phase. Post-banding acid suppression practices can vary; the explanation correctly frames its cited recommendation as conditional on no other indication, rather than forbidding all post-banding PPI use. Current guideline wording was not independently verified offline, and no confident clinical inaccuracy is asserted.

concept.learningObjective: Apply the high-risk early TIPS pathway even after apparently successful initial esophageal hemostasis.

record.title: Bleeding admission review
fairness: Pre-emptive covered TIPS is the best listed pathway for the stated Child-Pugh C11 patient in the early window after control of esophageal variceal bleeding. Serial banding plus nonselective beta blockade is a credible alternative for a different risk group; an elective distal splenorenal shunt is substantially less attractive in this decompensated setting.

The resident must recognize that initial hemostasis does not remove the high-risk indication and apply severity plus timing to choose early escalation. This is a high-yield, moderate two-step management decision. A documented Child-Pugh score is appropriate data because score reconstruction is not the task.

Although the presentation first describes a pre-endoscopy chart review, the current update clearly advances to the result and post-hemostasis assessment. The node contains all decision data and stands alone.

No nonclinical cue or confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The explanation appropriately describes TIPS assessment; it should not imply that the few listed workup findings replace complete candidacy evaluation. Contemporary eligibility guidance was not independently verified offline.

concept.displayName: Escalate recurrent variceal bleeding after adequate combined secondary prophylaxis.
concept.learningObjective: Escalate recurrent variceal bleeding after adequate combined secondary prophylaxis.

record.title: Recurrent bleeding review
fairness: TIPS is the best listed escalation pathway after recurrent esophageal variceal bleeding despite documented combined prevention. Switching beta blockers or increasing ligation frequency does not address the demonstrated failure as directly.

The two consequential judgments are to distinguish recurrence despite actual combined therapy from an adherence/omission problem, then select the next prevention strategy after acute control. This is high-yield and moderate; the required treatment history is clinical evidence, not an unfair giveaway.
The case is standalone, and the task clearly asks about prevention after the latest bleed is controlled. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical wording shortcut identified.

Tolerated nadolol does not quantify dose optimization, and the listed specialist findings are not an exhaustive TIPS assessment. These are limits of the vignette, not sufficient evidence that a different listed option is best. The explanation appropriately conditions the pathway on candidacy assessment; contemporary eligibility guidance was not independently verified offline.

fairness: Image-guided drainage is the best additional treatment for a persistently symptomatic enlarging liquefied liver cavity despite an active antibiotic, with a percutaneous route and no generalized peritonitis. Broadening antibiotics is a credible but insufficient source-control response; segmental resection is excessive without a supplied failure or anatomical indication.

The resident must distinguish antimicrobial susceptibility from effective source control, then choose the appropriate intervention based on cavity evolution and access. This is high-yield moderate reasoning. The access finding is decision-critical anatomy, not merely a sentence promising that the service is available.

The standalone case contains the initial infection record, treatment response and relevant imaging. It needs no absent companion or later drain-failure result. concept.displayName: Recognize complicated hepatic echinococcosis before selecting a percutaneous cyst pathway.
concept.learningObjective: Recognize complicated hepatic echinococcosis before selecting a percutaneous cyst pathway.

record.title: Cyst admission review
fairness: The daughter-cyst morphology and membrane-containing communicating biliary process support complicated hepatic echinococcosis. Specialist surgery with antiparasitic planning after stabilization is the best listed definitive pathway; communicating biliary disease makes PAIR an important but inappropriate competing shortcut, and medication with observation inadequately addresses the stated complication.

Two consequential steps are required: infer the disease and recognize that the demonstrated duct communication changes cyst-directed management after initial biliary decompression. This is a high-yield surgical complication/contraindication concept; hard is a qualitative prediction based on applying a less routine procedural boundary, not on obscure wording.

All three choices describe cyst-directed treatment at the same phase. The task distinguishes definitive cyst care from the antimicrobial/biliary care already underway, so the record is coherent and standalone. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonclinical cue identified.

The item does not supply enough anatomy to choose one exact cyst operation, and appropriately does not ask for one. Contemporary procedural guidance was not independently source-verified in this offline review.

choices.choiceLabel: Specialist hepatic cyst surgery with antiparasitic therapy

record.title: Growing nonavid nodule and biopsy-route anatomy
fairness: Matched CT technique and substantial interval growth must be weighed against a nonavid PET; the resident must then use airway access and bullae along needle trajectories to rank two plausible biopsy routes.

Navigational bronchoscopic sampling is the best offered plan. The bronchus-to-lesion relationship and percutaneous-path bullae are legitimate anatomical discriminators, not arbitrary permissions or diagnosis labels. Both routes require clinical knowledge to compare.

Local expertise and actual technical feasibility matter, as the explanation acknowledges. The item supports a favored offered route rather than a universal bronchoscopy rule, and does not claim that PET negativity proves benignity.
The chronology is independently specified; no previous nodule question is needed. The harder rating comes from two competing decisions, not missing information or numerical complexity.
suggestions: Preserve both the serial-imaging conflict and the route-specific anatomy. Do not simplify the explanation to 'PET can miss cancer' and thereby omit the second scored decision.

record.title: Tissue strategy for an invasive nodal mediastinal mass
fairness: Systemic symptoms, vessel relationships and additional nodes argue against treating location alone as proof of a readily resectable thymoma. The resident then must choose a tissue method that preserves architecture rather than cytology alone.

Core biopsy is the best offered initial plan. FNA is a credible specimen-choice error, while immediate complete thymectomy is inappropriate to assume from this invasive/nodal presentation. A later need for additional tissue would not negate the initial ranking.

The parasternal route establishes feasible pleura-sparing access for both needle options, so it does not select core over FNA by a unique permission cue. Normal AFP and beta-hCG are appropriately not treated as diagnostic proof.
suggestions: Preserve the distinction between a tissue-first strategy and the type of tissue required. Avoid turning the explanation into a blanket claim that any core biopsy will definitively classify every mediastinal lymphoma or other mass.

record.title: Retaining a functioning IPC during improving pleural infection
fairness: Cloudy fluid, fever and culture growth support infection rather than an isolated colonization result. The resident then must integrate treatment response, drainage function and the absence of tunnel findings to choose the catheter plan.
Continuing antibiotics with drainage through the functioning IPC is the defensible best option in this improving course. The explanation appropriately avoids an unconditional retain-the-device rule.

The later part is coherent with prior malignant effusion care and stands alone for the current device decision: it supplies IPC placement, infection observations, function and response. The earlier thoracentesis explanation does not rehearse this key. The intervening definitive-management decision is skipped but is not needed to solve this node.
suggestions: Retain the explicit later-course transition and the current infection/response observations. Do not expand earlier feedback to teach this catheter-retention answer before the later part is shown.

record.title: Initial nodal staging with a competing inflammatory explanation
fairness: The resident must avoid both treating PET uptake as proven metastasis and dismissing it as infection, then select the initial tissue-staging route for an accessible paratracheal node.

Systematic endosonographic sampling is the defensible preferred initial option. Mediastinoscopy is a credible tissue alternative rather than an absurd foil; repeat PET does not resolve histology before the proposed operation.

The absence of prior nodal sampling establishes the initial staging phase and does not uniquely select the key because two options obtain tissue. The explanation properly leaves the negative-endosonography follow-up outside this question rather than asserting a blanket subsequent operation.
suggestions: Preserve the initial-staging scope and accessible nodal location. Any later question about adequate negative endosonography needs its own current evidence and adequacy findings; this PASS does not decide that controversy.

record.title: Assessing symptom response before definitive pleural palliation
fairness: The small diagnostic sample establishes malignant fluid but leaves symptom contribution and expansion unresolved. COPD provides a real competing explanation for breathlessness rather than decorative comorbidity.

Therapeutic thoracentesis is the best offered next assessment before committing to a definitive pleural intervention. Talc and IPC are credible downstream alternatives, and the supplied unresolved response question makes this sequencing comparison fair.
The next node supplies a later IPC infection as a historical event. This explanation does not give away whether to retain or remove an infected catheter.
suggestions: Preserve the distinction between diagnostic sampling and therapeutic assessment. In the multipart case, keep the later IPC placement explicitly historical rather than implying that the learner's thoracentesis answer itself performed IPC placement.

record.title: Recurrent symptomatic malignant fluid with nonexpansion
fairness: Repeated symptom improvement establishes a meaningful drainage target; recurrent symptoms and the post-drainage anatomy then determine which ongoing strategy is most suitable. The air-fluid space is not used in isolation to diagnose nonexpandable lung.

Persistent broad separation with a visceral rind supports poor pleural apposition, making talc less suitable. Rapid recurrent symptomatic fluid, active ambulatory care and available catheter support favor IPC over repeated aspirations among these choices.

Repeat aspiration can remain reasonable with different goals or a very short anticipated course; the explanation correctly acknowledges this instead of declaring it universally wrong. No such competing constraint is supplied here.
The independent presentation supplies prior cytology, response trajectory and post-drainage findings, so this version does not depend on seeing the separately retained assessment node.
suggestions: Preserve the actual response trajectory and pleural observations, along with the limited explanation of why IPC is favored here. Do not convert this into an automatic treatment rule based on malignant cytology alone.

record.title: Treatment pathway after a malignant pleural result
fairness: The resident must recognize that a separate positive pleural result changes disease extent despite negative sampled mediastinal nodes, then select a systemic-treatment pathway rather than a local surgical or definitive locoregional plan.

Matched adenocarcinoma in adequate pleural cytology plus separate pleural nodules supports medical-oncology systemic-treatment planning. The explanation does not overstate negative nodal sampling as whole-mediastinal clearance or prescribe an unsupported drug regimen.

The standalone wrapper supplies the known lung primary, proposed operation and both relevant results. It does not require the preceding staging question to have been seen, and no earlier feedback within this case gives away the decision.
suggestions: Keep the two tissue compartments distinct and avoid adding a pre-answer metastatic-stage label. Preserve the pathway-level task rather than introducing regimen or exceptional local-treatment decisions without their necessary context.

record.title: Pleural drainage despite systemic improvement
fairness: The resident must distinguish improving systemic findings from persistent pleural infection requiring source control, then select initial catheter drainage rather than continued observation or immediate operative escalation.

The collection conditions make the low pH interpretable and the ultrasound supplies access information. These are needed for fairness, not gratuitous exclusions. Intercostal drainage is the defensible best initial option in the supplied record.
This is a standalone historical review, so its decision does not depend on a preceding diagnostic question. No later drain-malposition results are exposed here.
suggestions: Preserve the competing systemic trajectory and valid pleural-fluid result. The sentence about the founder reviewing source-control decisions can be shortened as nonessential framing, without changing the clinical decision.

record.title: Pneumothorax management after symptom reassessment
fairness: The chronology clearly separates limiting pain at arrival from minimal symptoms at the decision time. The resident must interpret that change and weigh it against persistent radiographic size before selecting management.

Under the named BTS approach, observation with follow-up is the best offered fit for the stable, minimally symptomatic patient who prefers home care. Aspiration is not universally wrong; the explanation appropriately limits its ranking to this patient and does not turn the constructed 3 cm measurement into an intervention threshold.

Home support, return access and preference are legitimate eligibility/context information here rather than a unique wording match to the key. The retrospective clinic frame and hospital reassessment task are coherent.
suggestions: Preserve the reassessment chronology, named guideline framework and preference-sensitive explanation. Do not change the feedback to claim that aspiration is categorically inappropriate.

record.title: Upfront thymectomy versus biopsy or limited excision
fairness: The resident must judge whether the solid thymic-bed lesion and preserved planes support an upfront resection strategy, then distinguish complete thymectomy from limited mass excision under the explicitly named guideline.

Complete thymectomy is the defensible best offered plan for the described high-probability localized thymic epithelial lesion. Normal markers and absent systemic symptoms do not prove histology; the explanation correctly states those limits.

The absence of prior tissue does not uniquely cue biopsy or resection; it creates the intended competing decision. The named guideline bounds a potentially practice-dependent comparison without specifying the correct operation in the task.
Although the presentation refers to prior MRI, its actual relevant findings are supplied in this singleton. It stands alone without the MRI-selection node.
suggestions: Preserve the named framework and the probabilistic language about likely pathology. Do not generalize this to all prevascular masses or imply that normal germ-cell markers exclude every alternative.

answerChoices.rationale: Her current symptoms are minimal and physiology is stable; BTS permits conservative management irrespective of radiographic size in this setting.

answerChoices.label: Needle aspiration followed by reassessment

record.title: Pneumothorax management after symptom reassessment
fairness: The chronology clearly separates limiting pain at arrival from minimal symptoms at the decision time. The resident must interpret that change and weigh it against persistent radiographic size before selecting management.

Under the named BTS approach, observation with follow-up is the best offered fit for the stable, minimally symptomatic patient who prefers home care. Aspiration is not universally wrong; the explanation appropriately limits its ranking to this patient and does not turn the constructed 3 cm measurement into an intervention threshold.

Home support, return access and preference are legitimate eligibility/context information here rather than a unique wording match to the key. The retrospective clinic frame and hospital reassessment task are coherent.
suggestions: Preserve the reassessment chronology, named guideline framework and preference-sensitive explanation. Do not change the feedback to claim that aspiration is categorically inappropriate.

record.title: Pleural drainage despite systemic improvement
fairness: The resident must distinguish improving systemic findings from persistent pleural infection requiring source control, then select initial catheter drainage rather than continued observation or immediate operative escalation.

The collection conditions make the low pH interpretable and the ultrasound supplies access information. These are needed for fairness, not gratuitous exclusions. Intercostal drainage is the defensible best initial option in the supplied record.
This is a standalone historical review, so its decision does not depend on a preceding diagnostic question. No later drain-malposition results are exposed here.
suggestions: Preserve the competing systemic trajectory and valid pleural-fluid result. The sentence about the founder reviewing source-control decisions can be shortened as nonessential framing, without changing the clinical decision.

decisionNodes.stem: Which pleural procedure should {patientName}'s hospital team arrange next?

answerChoices.label: Therapeutic ultrasound-guided thoracentesis
answerChoices.rationale: A therapeutic drainage trial can establish whether breathlessness improves and whether the lung expands before choosing a definitive device or pleurodesis.

answerChoices.label: Chest-tube insertion with talc pleurodesis
answerChoices.rationale: The cytology establishes malignancy but not the functional or expansion prerequisites for this definitive approach.

answerChoices.label: Tunneled indwelling pleural catheter placement
answerChoices.rationale: An IPC is a credible later option, but the represented record has not separated COPD-related symptoms from fluid contribution or characterized lung expansion.

decisionNodes.explanation: A small diagnostic sample answers whether malignant cells are present; it does not test the effect of draining the effusion. Therapeutic thoracentesis can assess both symptom contribution and expansion. The later definitive choice should use those observations.

items.label: Current record

answerChoices.rationale: The device provides effective drainage and the infection is improving; routine removal would remove useful source control.

answerChoices.rationale: The represented functioning catheter and improving course do not support automatic removal merely because the pleural culture is positive.

answerChoices.label: Exchange the IPC and continue antibiotics
answerChoices.rationale: No mechanical failure or persistent infectious course is shown to justify an immediate exchange.

question.explanation: A small diagnostic sample answers whether malignant cells are present; it does not test the effect of draining the effusion. Therapeutic thoracentesis can assess both symptom contribution and expansion. The later definitive choice should use those observations.

concept.displayName: Use a therapeutic drainage trial when a diagnostic-only sample has not established response or expansion.
concept.learningObjective: Use a therapeutic drainage trial when a diagnostic-only sample has not established response or expansion.

record.title: Assessing symptom response before definitive pleural palliation
fairness: The small diagnostic sample establishes malignant fluid but leaves symptom contribution and expansion unresolved. COPD provides a real competing explanation for breathlessness rather than decorative comorbidity.

Therapeutic thoracentesis is the best offered next assessment before committing to a definitive pleural intervention. Talc and IPC are credible downstream alternatives, and the supplied unresolved response question makes this sequencing comparison fair.
The next node supplies a later IPC infection as a historical event. This explanation does not give away whether to retain or remove an infected catheter.
suggestions: Preserve the distinction between diagnostic sampling and therapeutic assessment. In the multipart case, keep the later IPC placement explicitly historical rather than implying that the learner's thoracentesis answer itself performed IPC placement.

concept.displayName: Retain a functioning pleural catheter during responding infection treatment.
concept.learningObjective: Retain a functioning pleural catheter during responding infection treatment.

record.title: Retaining a functioning IPC during improving pleural infection
fairness: Cloudy fluid, fever and culture growth support infection rather than an isolated colonization result. The resident then must integrate treatment response, drainage function and the absence of tunnel findings to choose the catheter plan.
Continuing antibiotics with drainage through the functioning IPC is the defensible best option in this improving course. The explanation appropriately avoids an unconditional retain-the-device rule.

The later part is coherent with prior malignant effusion care and stands alone for the current device decision: it supplies IPC placement, infection observations, function and response. The earlier thoracentesis explanation does not rehearse this key. The intervening definitive-management decision is skipped but is not needed to solve this node.
suggestions: Retain the explicit later-course transition and the current infection/response observations. Do not expand earlier feedback to teach this catheter-retention answer before the later part is shown.

answerChoices.label: Tunneled indwelling pleural catheter placement
answerChoices.rationale: Repeated symptomatic benefit identifies a useful drainage target; persistent nonapposition makes an IPC preferable to attempting talc pleurodesis.

answerChoices.label: Chest-tube talc slurry pleurodesis
answerChoices.rationale: Talc depends on adequate pleural apposition. Persistent broad separation with a visceral rind makes successful apposition unlikely in this record.

answerChoices.label: Repeat therapeutic thoracentesis when symptomatic
answerChoices.rationale: This can palliate symptoms, but repeated rapid reaccumulation has already required two procedures. An accepted definitive drainage option is preferable in this ongoing-care context.

decisionNodes.explanation: {patientName} repeatedly breathes better after fluid removal, so this effusion is a meaningful symptom target. The persistent large pleural separation, patent central bronchi and visceral rind together support nonexpandable lung; the air-fluid space alone would not establish that conclusion. An IPC can provide ongoing drainage without requiring the apposition needed for talc pleurodesis. Repeat aspiration remains a patient-specific option, but the two episodes of rapid symptomatic recurrence and feasible catheter care favor IPC among these plans. The choice requires discussion of burden and goals; it is not a universal rule based on cytology alone.

items.label: Discussion
items.value: She is willing to consider the listed approaches. Community catheter care is available; no approach has been ruled out by preference.

concept.displayName: Choose durable pleural palliation from actual symptomatic response and nonapposition.
concept.learningObjective: Choose durable pleural palliation from actual symptomatic response and nonapposition.

record.title: Recurrent symptomatic malignant fluid with nonexpansion
fairness: Repeated symptom improvement establishes a meaningful drainage target; recurrent symptoms and the post-drainage anatomy then determine which ongoing strategy is most suitable. The air-fluid space is not used in isolation to diagnose nonexpandable lung.

Persistent broad separation with a visceral rind supports poor pleural apposition, making talc less suitable. Rapid recurrent symptomatic fluid, active ambulatory care and available catheter support favor IPC over repeated aspirations among these choices.

Repeat aspiration can remain reasonable with different goals or a very short anticipated course; the explanation correctly acknowledges this instead of declaring it universally wrong. No such competing constraint is supplied here.
The independent presentation supplies prior cytology, response trajectory and post-drainage findings, so this version does not depend on seeing the separately retained assessment node.
suggestions: Preserve the actual response trajectory and pleural observations, along with the limited explanation of why IPC is favored here. Do not convert this into an automatic treatment rule based on malignant cytology alone.

record.title: Initial nodal staging with a competing inflammatory explanation
fairness: The resident must avoid both treating PET uptake as proven metastasis and dismissing it as infection, then select the initial tissue-staging route for an accessible paratracheal node.

Systematic endosonographic sampling is the defensible preferred initial option. Mediastinoscopy is a credible tissue alternative rather than an absurd foil; repeat PET does not resolve histology before the proposed operation.

The absence of prior nodal sampling establishes the initial staging phase and does not uniquely select the key because two options obtain tissue. The explanation properly leaves the negative-endosonography follow-up outside this question rather than asserting a blanket subsequent operation.
suggestions: Preserve the initial-staging scope and accessible nodal location. Any later question about adequate negative endosonography needs its own current evidence and adequacy findings; this PASS does not decide that controversy.

record.title: Treatment pathway after a malignant pleural result
fairness: The resident must recognize that a separate positive pleural result changes disease extent despite negative sampled mediastinal nodes, then select a systemic-treatment pathway rather than a local surgical or definitive locoregional plan.

Matched adenocarcinoma in adequate pleural cytology plus separate pleural nodules supports medical-oncology systemic-treatment planning. The explanation does not overstate negative nodal sampling as whole-mediastinal clearance or prescribe an unsupported drug regimen.

The standalone wrapper supplies the known lung primary, proposed operation and both relevant results. It does not require the preceding staging question to have been seen, and no earlier feedback within this case gives away the decision.
suggestions: Keep the two tissue compartments distinct and avoid adding a pre-answer metastatic-stage label. Preserve the pathway-level task rather than introducing regimen or exceptional local-treatment decisions without their necessary context.

decisionNodes.stem: Which next diagnostic plan best fits {patientName}'s serial nodule findings and access anatomy?

answerChoices.label: Navigational bronchoscopy with nodule sampling
answerChoices.rationale: The serial CT change remains concerning despite nonavid PET. A bronchus entering the lesion supports a bronchoscopic route, while bullae make the percutaneous paths less attractive.

answerChoices.label: CT-guided percutaneous nodule core biopsy
answerChoices.rationale: Tissue investigation is appropriate, but the available needle paths cross bullous emphysema and carry greater pneumothorax concern than the available airway route.

answerChoices.label: Short-interval diagnostic chest CT surveillance
answerChoices.rationale: Nonavid PET does not erase the substantial dimensional increase on comparable scans over the stated interval. Continued imaging alone leaves that concerning trajectory unresolved.

decisionNodes.explanation: The dated matched CT studies show a substantial size increase over nine months. A nonavid PET cannot establish benignity of that lesion. Further diagnostic investigation is therefore appropriate among these choices. A bronchus entering the nodule supports bronchoscopic sampling, with navigation used to aid access; bullous emphysema on the available transthoracic paths increases pneumothorax concern. Those findings favor the offered bronchoscopic plan over reflexive percutaneous sampling. Route selection still depends on local expertise and individual anatomy, and is not a universal rule for all peripheral nodules.

record.title: Growing nonavid nodule and biopsy-route anatomy
fairness: Matched CT technique and substantial interval growth must be weighed against a nonavid PET; the resident must then use airway access and bullae along needle trajectories to rank two plausible biopsy routes.

Navigational bronchoscopic sampling is the best offered plan. The bronchus-to-lesion relationship and percutaneous-path bullae are legitimate anatomical discriminators, not arbitrary permissions or diagnosis labels. Both routes require clinical knowledge to compare.

Local expertise and actual technical feasibility matter, as the explanation acknowledges. The item supports a favored offered route rather than a universal bronchoscopy rule, and does not claim that PET negativity proves benignity.
The chronology is independently specified; no previous nodule question is needed. The harder rating comes from two competing decisions, not missing information or numerical complexity.
suggestions: Preserve both the serial-imaging conflict and the route-specific anatomy. Do not simplify the explanation to 'PET can miss cancer' and thereby omit the second scored decision.

decisionNodes.stem: Under the SEOM thymic-tumour guideline, which procedural plan best fits {patientName}'s current work-up?

answerChoices.label: Complete thymectomy with intact lesion removal
answerChoices.rationale: The pattern favors a localized resectable thymic epithelial lesion. Complete thymectomy includes the lesion and remaining thymus rather than limited mass excision.

answerChoices.label: Limited lesion excision with thymus preservation
answerChoices.rationale: This is a distinct operation, but the specified guideline prefers complete thymectomy for the suspected resectable thymic epithelial tumour scenario.

answerChoices.label: Percutaneous core biopsy before treatment selection
answerChoices.rationale: Biopsy is appropriate when histology is needed to choose treatment, but it is not mandatory for a highly probable completely resectable thymic epithelial lesion.

decisionNodes.explanation: The solid enhancing thymic-bed lesion, preserved tissue planes and lack of separate nodal or pleural disease favor a localized resectable thymic epithelial tumour. These observations do not prove histology, and normal AFP and beta-hCG do not exclude all alternatives. In this high-probability resectable scenario, the SEOM guideline permits upfront surgery without mandatory biopsy and prefers complete thymectomy, including residual thymus and perithymic fat, over mass-only excision. Invasive or atypical disease would change the tissue-first decision.

record.title: Upfront thymectomy versus biopsy or limited excision
fairness: The resident must judge whether the solid thymic-bed lesion and preserved planes support an upfront resection strategy, then distinguish complete thymectomy from limited mass excision under the explicitly named guideline.

Complete thymectomy is the defensible best offered plan for the described high-probability localized thymic epithelial lesion. Normal markers and absent systemic symptoms do not prove histology; the explanation correctly states those limits.

The absence of prior tissue does not uniquely cue biopsy or resection; it creates the intended competing decision. The named guideline bounds a potentially practice-dependent comparison without specifying the correct operation in the task.
Although the presentation refers to prior MRI, its actual relevant findings are supplied in this singleton. It stands alone without the MRI-selection node.
suggestions: Preserve the named framework and the probabilistic language about likely pathology. Do not generalize this to all prevascular masses or imply that normal germ-cell markers exclude every alternative.

answerChoices.label: Image-guided fine-needle mediastinal aspiration
answerChoices.rationale: Cytology can be less suitable than core tissue for the required mediastinal tumour distinction; the guideline does not generally recommend FNA for this work-up.

record.title: Tissue strategy for an invasive nodal mediastinal mass
fairness: Systemic symptoms, vessel relationships and additional nodes argue against treating location alone as proof of a readily resectable thymoma. The resident then must choose a tissue method that preserves architecture rather than cytology alone.

Core biopsy is the best offered initial plan. FNA is a credible specimen-choice error, while immediate complete thymectomy is inappropriate to assume from this invasive/nodal presentation. A later need for additional tissue would not negate the initial ranking.

The parasternal route establishes feasible pleura-sparing access for both needle options, so it does not select core over FNA by a unique permission cue. Normal AFP and beta-hCG are appropriately not treated as diagnostic proof.
suggestions: Preserve the distinction between a tissue-first strategy and the type of tissue required. Avoid turning the explanation into a blanket claim that any core biopsy will definitively classify every mediastinal lymphoma or other mass.

record.title: Treatment of active humoral injury after steroid nonresponse
fairness: Plasma exchange with IVIG is the best listed additional treatment backbone for the represented microvascular inflammation, C4d and donor-specific antibodies, without the described cellular or chronic glomerular component. The explanation appropriately labels the comparative evidence as weak.

The resident must reinterpret the repeat tissue rather than infer refractory cellular rejection from steroid failure, then choose mechanism-directed treatment. ATG is a credible anchoring error; maintenance reduction is an infection-pathway error.

The capillary findings and antibodies are necessary clinical observations, not a diagnosis label or direct phrase match to plasma exchange. Multiple negatives make the item moderate rather than hard but keep the competing treatment boundaries fair.
The standalone update supplies the prior course, current biopsy and background maintenance optimization. It does not depend on the earlier cellular rescue case.

Absence of glomerular double contours alone should not be taught as excluding every possible chronic AMR lesion. The text is limited to the represented tissue rather than a complete Banff classification; no confident key-changing inaccuracy is identified within this option set.
suggestions: Preserve the weak-evidence and acute-active scope qualifications; do not extend this backbone claim to all chronic active AMR.

record.title: Cytopenias after adding allopurinol to azathioprine
fairness: Stopping allopurinol is the best listed additional medication change while the service addresses cytopenias and the azathioprine regimen. Substitution with febuxostat preserves the important xanthine-oxidase interaction concern; reducing tacrolimus does not address the represented temporal pattern.

The resident identifies the interaction from chronology and then avoids a same-class substitution error. The febuxostat alternative gives this high-yield drug interaction more than simple culprit recognition.

The task's 'additional' wording is justified by the shared active assessment of azathioprine; it does not mean stopping allopurinol is the complete cytopenia management plan. No option is a uniquely cautious composite answer.

The standalone update explicitly supplies the regimen, added medicine and blood-count changes; 'A later record' is understandable without the former pregnancy companion. The explanation appropriately acknowledges management-strategy differences without inventing a dose.

record.title: Biopsy-supported BK nephropathy: treatment direction
fairness: Stepwise maintenance reduction is the best listed direction given persistent plasma detection, tissue inclusions/staining, low immunologic risk and the represented absence of concurrent rejection. Steroid escalation and cidofovir are not equally supported routine alternatives in this setting.

The resident interprets tissue plus blood findings and applies the infection-versus-rejection balance to treatment. This remains moderate, not hard: the integrated exclusion of rejection reduces competing uncertainty.
No reliable wording, length, absolute or convergence shortcut selects the key. Low immunologic risk is a necessary treatment boundary, although it is supplied as a clinical summary.

The later admission follows the first BK node coherently and includes all findings necessary for independent selection. Earlier feedback scaffolds compartment interpretation but does not give this treatment answer.
suggestions: Keep the low-risk and no-concurrent-rejection boundaries attached to this version; do not generalize its treatment to every BK-positive recipient.

record.title: Renewed graft dysfunction after BK treatment
fairness: Repeat allograft biopsy is the best listed cause-defining plan before increasing or further decreasing maintenance therapy. Prior biopsy-proven BK and subsequent plasma clearance do not identify the cause of renewed dysfunction.

The resident must interpret the discordance between viral and renal trajectories, then avoid opposite empiric immunosuppression changes with different hazards. The prior initial improvement is useful chronology, not decorative detail.

The biopsy choice is the only investigation, but this does not automatically invalidate the option set: the case supplies a real unresolved discrepancy that determines whether an empiric drug change is justified. 'Graft-assessment plan' mildly favors evaluation; it is not a deterministic match because the other plans also include follow-up creatinine.

The standalone node includes the prior biopsy, treatment, response and new deterioration. The earlier BK case need not be seen. This is high-yield graft dysfunction reasoning with no asserted universal BK threshold.
suggestions: Use a neutral lead-in such as 'Which next plan best fits the renewed graft dysfunction?' to avoid even the mild investigation bias from 'graft-assessment plan'.

record.title: Isolated BK viruria and maintenance treatment
fairness: Maintaining the regimen with repeat plasma testing is the best listed plan for urinary detection with negative contemporaneous plasma testing and stable function. No unsupported numerical treatment threshold or interval is asserted.

Interpreting specimen compartments and then deciding whether to accept rejection risk from maintenance reduction are consequential steps. Immediate reduction is a credible error; leflunomide is a weaker treatment misconception.
All choices share 'repeat plasma BK testing', so that phrase does not disclose the key. The result and stable function require clinical interpretation rather than grammatical elimination.
First part is self-contained. Its explanation teaches the significance of the present urinary finding without naming the later biopsy-proven treatment.

record.title: Escalation after persistent cellular graft injury
fairness: Rabbit antithymocyte globulin is the best listed escalation for continued deterioration after completed steroids with repeat cellular injury and the represented negative viral/humoral reassessment. The phrasing 'consider' avoids an unconditional rescue prescription.

Two consequential steps remain: reclassify persistent injury using repeat tissue rather than steroid nonresponse alone, then select cellular rescue instead of humoral treatment or maintenance reduction. This is high-yield rejection management.

The summary 'does not support an antibody-mediated component' makes elimination easier, but still requires knowledge of the competing treatments; it does not create a nonmedical unique-word match. The specific treatment choices are comparable.
The standalone update includes prior steroid treatment and repeat findings; the opening 'A later record' does not require another scored question to establish the timeline.

record.title: Initial therapy for untreated cellular graft injury
fairness: Intravenous methylprednisolone is the best listed initial treatment for the represented untreated interstitial/tubular cellular process without the described arterial, viral or humoral component. The explicit arterial sampling repairs an important severity ambiguity without inventing a Banff grade.
The resident interprets the biopsy and competing infection/humoral findings, then distinguishes initial steroid therapy from lymphocyte-depleting rescue. These are consequential high-yield decisions.

The negatives are extensive and lower difficulty, but they establish relevant treatment boundaries; there is no key-only wording overlap or option-length advantage. The task prespecifies antirejection treatment appropriately for choosing among three such regimens.

The current update retains persistent dysfunction and the treatment-naive stage, so the standalone node no longer needs a preceding biopsy-selection question. No confident clinical inaccuracy is identified; exact pathology/severity ranking still needs clinician sign-off.
suggestions: Consider tightening the report wording without removing the represented arterial assessment, infection studies or initial-treatment boundary.

record.title: Medication adjustment during CMV-associated treatment neutropenia
fairness: Temporarily holding mycophenolate while retaining renal-adjusted valganciclovir is the best listed interim plan for the specified neutropenia during unfinished treatment, with low immunologic risk and count support/reassessment being arranged.

The resident interprets the neutrophil trajectory in a multiple-drug setting, then preserves antiviral treatment exposure while addressing another marrow suppressant. Lowering an otherwise appropriate treatment dose or treating active disease with letermovir are not equally supported alternatives.

The count trend supplies a meaningful problem rather than merely 'falling white cells'. No exact universal hold threshold is inferred from these constructed values. The explanation appropriately avoids asserting that mycophenolate is the proven sole cause.

The specific medication plans are comparably framed. 'Low' immunologic risk and 'appropriate' renal dosing are supplied judgments that narrow the choice but are necessary fairness boundaries here, not a nonmedical key match.

The standalone node includes current infection status, regimen, renal function and graft-risk context; it does not rely on the preceding CMV route question. This is high-yield competing drug-toxicity and treatment-efficacy reasoning.
suggestions: Keep the temporary/interim wording and explicit reassessment; do not turn this option into an automatic mycophenolate-stop rule for every declining count.

record.title: CMV discharge therapy: route and treatment phase
fairness: Oral valganciclovir at renal-adjusted treatment dosing is the best listed discharge plan with improving gastrointestinal symptoms, demonstrated oral intake and persistent quantifiable CMV above the stated endpoint. Continued treatment does not itself require IV delivery.

Two consequential distinctions remain: infer adequate oral delivery from the clinical response, then distinguish unfinished treatment from prevention. The balanced four-cell matrix does not select the key by majority-component convergence.

'Scheduled oral medicines taken without vomiting' supports two oral options, while the unfinished virologic course supports two treatment-dose options. Neither phrase uniquely identifies the answer without integrating both observations. The intake observations are decision-critical, not gratuitous permission.

The standalone update contains the diagnosis, initial severe delivery problem, improvement and remaining treatment indication. The task is complete. No universal viral-load endpoint is invented; clinician review should retain the represented clinical improvement when accepting the route switch.

record.title: Persistent gastrointestinal symptoms with negative plasma CMV testing
fairness: Ileocolonoscopy with mucosal biopsy best distinguishes the represented mucosal differential, including tissue-invasive CMV and medication injury. Repeated negative blood testing does not settle tissue disease. A cellular-immunity assay does not provide a competing tissue diagnosis.

The resident must reject false reassurance from blood testing and choose a test that distinguishes remaining mucosal causes. This is a useful transplant infection decision; the two other blood-focused choices make it moderate rather than hard.

No direct lexical cue names the biopsy. The repeated plasma assay is a weaker distractor because it has already been performed, but it still represents a recognizable mistaken reliance on blood surveillance. Do not count its repetition as an independent hard discriminator.

The standalone update includes persistent symptoms, prior tests, medication and structural context. 'Antiviral treatment records' in the presentation anticipates the broader record but neither establishes the cause of this episode nor supplies the investigation.
suggestions: For a future harder variant, compare tissue evaluation with a genuinely plausible competing diagnostic or medication strategy; do not add more negative tests just to lengthen the stem.

record.title: Persistent delayed graft function after an earlier tubular-injury biopsy
fairness: Repeat allograft sampling is the best listed next assessment for persistent dialysis dependence/nonrecovery after an earlier tubular-injury specimen and the represented reassessment of reversible contributors. The earlier biopsy does not establish the current cause.

The resident interprets the age and limited temporal scope of tissue evidence, then decides to reassess rather than anchor on tubular injury or treat presumed rejection empirically. This is a high-yield delayed-function decision.

The supportive-care sentence applies to all options, preventing the biopsy answer from being the only comprehensive plan. 'Graft-assessment plan' mildly favors investigation, but monitoring is also an assessment strategy and the unresolved course justifies comparing assessment with empiric therapy.

The day-3/day-11 sequence is explicit and standalone. The explanation treats the dates as a constructed example and acknowledges low-quality interval-biopsy evidence rather than declaring a universal mandatory biopsy day.

Individual biopsy timing can vary with risk and prior findings; this offline review does not independently verify current interval guidance. Within the represented persistent nonrecovery and offered choices, no competing option is equally compelling.
suggestions: A neutral 'Which next plan best fits the postoperative course?' would remove the mild assessment-language bias without changing the clinical information.

record.title: Tacrolimus during recovering delayed graft function
fairness: Continuing the represented tacrolimus regimen is the best listed plan given improving output/creatinine, tissue-supported tubular injury and verified target-range exposure. Earlier dialysis alone does not establish ongoing CNI toxicity or justify a routine switch to sirolimus.

The resident interprets the recovery trajectory against the earlier dialysis requirement, then decides whether the existing regimen needs alteration. This is a practical high-yield distinction between delayed function and an indication to withdraw immunosuppression.

Continue/withhold/replace options are parallel specific plans. The target-range result is relevant but is not presented as universally excluding CNI injury. No reliable nonmedical cue selects the key.
The case is now standalone and includes the biopsy and trajectory it requires; 'subsequent biopsy' does not leave a decision-critical prior result missing.

record.title: Progressing lymphadenopathy despite falling EBV DNA
fairness: Representative lymph-node tissue is the best listed cause-defining investigation for enlarging/multisite nodes after a nondiagnostic aspirate. A falling blood EBV result cannot classify the lesion; PET/CT may later assist staging but does not replace tissue diagnosis.

The consequential reasoning is to reconcile discordant blood and lesion trajectories, then choose a diagnostic specimen rather than repeat surveillance or move directly to staging. This is a high-yield PTLD and lymphoma diagnostic principle.

The aspirate's inability to classify the process is necessary adequacy evidence rather than an invented missing-test cue. The choices are investigations of comparable specificity without a key-only explanatory qualifier.
The current standalone case supplies the earlier sampling result, subsequent progression and transplant context. It does not depend on removed companion nodes.

record.title: Persistent allograft dysfunction: cause-defining investigation
fairness: Kidney-allograft core biopsy is the best listed investigation after persistent dysfunction despite volume correction and the represented structural assessment. Plasma BK testing remains useful concurrently; the item does not need to imply that it should be omitted.

The resident must interpret the residual unexplained dysfunction, then choose tissue classification rather than equate missed doses with rejection. The alternatives are parallel investigations. Necessary flow, drainage and exposure findings do not yield a reliable nonmedical phrase match.
The current single-node case stands alone; its presentation supplies age and sex and its task specifies persistent graft dysfunction. No later executable treatment node remains in this case.

Review scope: all 19 current executable candidates (17 new and 2 rewrites), including the 8 preserved candidate versions, were independently assessed from presentation, update, task, options and explanation. No separate exhibit is present. The original 3 kept records, 29 proposed retired/replacement input records, held/unkeyed material and 4 parked corrections are noted but excluded from verdicts. Review-only keys and author gate claims were not evidence of quality.

This is an offline editorial review, not source verification or clinical approval. PASS does not change needs_clinician_review or replace Melissa Rowland's exact-version sign-off. Difficulty and highYield are qualitative judgments, not measured performance or verified examination-frequency claims. Runtime rendering, randomization and wait metadata are outside this visible-text review.
suggestions: Preserve the distinction between prioritizing biopsy and also obtaining indicated viral tests.

record.title: Renewed dysfunction after correction of a tacrolimus interaction
fairness: Allograft tissue is the best listed next step after the earlier exposure problem improves and renal dysfunction subsequently recurs despite valid target-range levels and the represented initial assessment. Neither further reduction nor restoration of the earlier dose follows from creatinine alone.

The resident must separate the earlier drug-interaction episode from the current unexplained course, then choose tissue assessment rather than another unsupported dose-direction change. This meets two-step reasoning and tests a high-yield anchoring error.

The different plan types are justified by a genuine unresolved causal discrepancy. The task does not name biopsy, and the explanation expressly avoids claiming that a target trough excludes all CNI injury or that dose reduction proves rejection.

The standalone chronology is coherent and complete. The interaction facts support the earlier episode rather than diagnose the renewed decline. This substantially overlaps the general renal-biopsy construct, which is a coverage consideration rather than a fairness failure.
suggestions: Keep the initial response followed by renewed deterioration; shortening this to a single high tacrolimus concentration would change the decision.

record.title: Tacrolimus dosing after a mistimed concentration
fairness: Continuing the monitored current dose while obtaining a valid predose level is the best listed plan given a postdose sample, unchanged renal function, no represented toxicity symptoms and no other medication change. The flagged value does not establish an excessive trough.

The resident interprets sampling validity and then uses the stable clinical course to choose continuation rather than precautionary dose reduction or withholding. The added treatment decision is consequential; it is not merely choosing the definition of a trough.

The shared repeat-level clause in all three choices prevents monitoring wording from identifying the answer. The explicitly stated postdose timing is necessary data, not an unfair disclosure of the dose decision.

The standalone update supplies timing, clinical trajectory and the imminent dosing decision. This is a common medication-monitoring pitfall. Its difficulty is toward the easier end of moderate; no numerical toxicity threshold is asserted.
suggestions: Preserve the stable-function and symptom context so the answer is not generalized to an ill patient merely because one specimen was mistimed.

record.title: Persistent allograft dysfunction: cause-defining investigation
fairness: Kidney-allograft core biopsy is the best listed investigation after persistent dysfunction despite volume correction and the represented structural assessment. Plasma BK testing remains useful concurrently; the item does not need to imply that it should be omitted.

The resident must interpret the residual unexplained dysfunction, then choose tissue classification rather than equate missed doses with rejection. The alternatives are parallel investigations. Necessary flow, drainage and exposure findings do not yield a reliable nonmedical phrase match.
The current single-node case stands alone; its presentation supplies age and sex and its task specifies persistent graft dysfunction. No later executable treatment node remains in this case.

Review scope: all 19 current executable candidates (17 new and 2 rewrites), including the 8 preserved candidate versions, were independently assessed from presentation, update, task, options and explanation. No separate exhibit is present. The original 3 kept records, 29 proposed retired/replacement input records, held/unkeyed material and 4 parked corrections are noted but excluded from verdicts. Review-only keys and author gate claims were not evidence of quality.

This is an offline editorial review, not source verification or clinical approval. PASS does not change needs_clinician_review or replace Melissa Rowland's exact-version sign-off. Difficulty and highYield are qualitative judgments, not measured performance or verified examination-frequency claims. Runtime rendering, randomization and wait metadata are outside this visible-text review.
suggestions: Preserve the distinction between prioritizing biopsy and also obtaining indicated viral tests.

record.title: Escalation after persistent cellular graft injury
fairness: Rabbit antithymocyte globulin is the best listed escalation for continued deterioration after completed steroids with repeat cellular injury and the represented negative viral/humoral reassessment. The phrasing 'consider' avoids an unconditional rescue prescription.

Two consequential steps remain: reclassify persistent injury using repeat tissue rather than steroid nonresponse alone, then select cellular rescue instead of humoral treatment or maintenance reduction. This is high-yield rejection management.

The summary 'does not support an antibody-mediated component' makes elimination easier, but still requires knowledge of the competing treatments; it does not create a nonmedical unique-word match. The specific treatment choices are comparable.
The standalone update includes prior steroid treatment and repeat findings; the opening 'A later record' does not require another scored question to establish the timeline.

record.title: Isolated BK viruria and maintenance treatment
fairness: Maintaining the regimen with repeat plasma testing is the best listed plan for urinary detection with negative contemporaneous plasma testing and stable function. No unsupported numerical treatment threshold or interval is asserted.

Interpreting specimen compartments and then deciding whether to accept rejection risk from maintenance reduction are consequential steps. Immediate reduction is a credible error; leflunomide is a weaker treatment misconception.
All choices share 'repeat plasma BK testing', so that phrase does not disclose the key. The result and stable function require clinical interpretation rather than grammatical elimination.
First part is self-contained. Its explanation teaches the significance of the present urinary finding without naming the later biopsy-proven treatment.

record.title: Biopsy-supported BK nephropathy: treatment direction
fairness: Stepwise maintenance reduction is the best listed direction given persistent plasma detection, tissue inclusions/staining, low immunologic risk and the represented absence of concurrent rejection. Steroid escalation and cidofovir are not equally supported routine alternatives in this setting.

The resident interprets tissue plus blood findings and applies the infection-versus-rejection balance to treatment. This remains moderate, not hard: the integrated exclusion of rejection reduces competing uncertainty.
No reliable wording, length, absolute or convergence shortcut selects the key. Low immunologic risk is a necessary treatment boundary, although it is supplied as a clinical summary.

The later admission follows the first BK node coherently and includes all findings necessary for independent selection. Earlier feedback scaffolds compartment interpretation but does not give this treatment answer.
suggestions: Keep the low-risk and no-concurrent-rejection boundaries attached to this version; do not generalize its treatment to every BK-positive recipient.

record.title: Progressing lymphadenopathy despite falling EBV DNA
fairness: Representative lymph-node tissue is the best listed cause-defining investigation for enlarging/multisite nodes after a nondiagnostic aspirate. A falling blood EBV result cannot classify the lesion; PET/CT may later assist staging but does not replace tissue diagnosis.

The consequential reasoning is to reconcile discordant blood and lesion trajectories, then choose a diagnostic specimen rather than repeat surveillance or move directly to staging. This is a high-yield PTLD and lymphoma diagnostic principle.

The aspirate's inability to classify the process is necessary adequacy evidence rather than an invented missing-test cue. The choices are investigations of comparable specificity without a key-only explanatory qualifier.
The current standalone case supplies the earlier sampling result, subsequent progression and transplant context. It does not depend on removed companion nodes.

Obtain tissue histology with CMV immunohistochemistry and evaluate competing mucosal causes. The story does not diagnose CMV from diarrhea itself. The tissue result establishes CMV organ disease, and the recorded vomiting and gastrointestinal severity make oral exposure unreliable. Initial intravenous ganciclovir is favored; the treating service adjusts for kidney function. No dose or duration is authored. With renal dosing verified and active treatment still required, avoid reducing antiviral exposure solely because of leukopenia. The treating teams can address other marrow-suppressive therapy and blood-count support. The exact cytopenia response remains a specialist decision.
