concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish clearance of the local invasive-polyp site from the regional oncologic question created by adverse invasive histology.

concepts.displayName: Continence history before irreversible sphincter division
concepts.learningObjective: Reassess a proposed lateral internal sphincterotomy when baseline leakage and sphincter-injury history put the patient outside the represented low-continence-risk scenario.

concepts.displayName: Matching esophageal provocation to unexplained food symptoms
concepts.learningObjective: Select symptom-matched solid-meal manometry provocation when an adequate ordinary water-swallow series does not explain food-associated obstruction symptoms.

concepts.displayName: Coverage when the recipient bed cannot support a graft
concepts.learningObjective: Choose a reconstructive approach that transfers perfused tissue when the recipient bed cannot support avascular skin transfer.

concepts.displayName: Perfusion after a completely detached tissue transfer
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the vascular reconnection needed by a completely detached vessel-bearing flap rather than apply graft or pedicled-flap assumptions.

concepts.displayName: Operative contamination and a later wound infection
concepts.learningObjective: Keep contamination class at the operation separate from a subsequent surgical-site infection when reconciling wound documentation.

concepts.displayName: A local contrast event despite an allergy label
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a localized injection-site contrast event from a generalized allergic-like event using the actual distribution and timing.

concepts.displayName: T-cell suppression does not establish antibody-pathway control
concepts.learningObjective: Do not use tacrolimus's T-cell target to exclude a separately supported preformed-antibody vascular mechanism in graft injury.

concepts.displayName: Urgent findings override an elective optimization plan
concepts.learningObjective: Change an elective incisional-hernia optimization plan when acute irreducibility and obstructive/peritoneal findings develop.

concepts.displayName: Irreversible limb findings and the proposed intervention
concepts.learningObjective: Use a complete irreversible acute-ischemia examination to reject attempted revascularization and obtain vascular assessment of a non-salvage pathway.

concepts.displayName: Reassurance after a negative test
concepts.learningObjective: Calculate negative predictive value using everyone with a negative test rather than all reference-negative or all reference-positive participants.

concepts.displayName: Comparing positive-result frequency across reference groups
concepts.learningObjective: Calculate a positive likelihood ratio as the positive-test probability with the condition divided by that probability without it.

concepts.displayName: Absolute adverse-event increase and number needed to harm
concepts.learningObjective: Calculate number needed to harm from an absolute adverse-event increase with the comparator and follow-up horizon retained.

concepts.displayName: A paired binary change needs a paired analysis
concepts.learningObjective: Choose McNemar analysis for repeated binary observations in the same patients rather than treat the before and after groups as independent.

concepts.displayName: Equivalence requires the prespecified margin comparison
concepts.learningObjective: Use the protocol-specified equivalence interval rule rather than a nonsignificant zero-difference test to judge equivalence.

concepts.displayName: Comparing outcomes at a common surgical case mix
concepts.learningObjective: Calculate directly standardized outcome risks using a common specified stratum distribution rather than compare crude rates from different case mixes.

concepts.displayName: Investigate a secondary junction lesion despite achalasia-pattern physiology
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate positional motor findings with a discordant wall abnormality and select etiologic assessment before attributing the pattern to primary achalasia.

concepts.displayName: Do not equate reduced reserve with an outflow-treatment indication
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a recovery-integral finding separately from junction pressure behavior and select complementary emptying assessment rather than unsupported dilation.

concepts.displayName: Request a symptom-matched dynamic groin acquisition
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish musculoskeletal and posture-dependent groin observations and choose the targeted ultrasound acquisition rather than a generic modality escalation.

concepts.displayName: Recognize the femoral exception to inguinal watchful waiting
concepts.learningObjective: Use current vascular/ligament landmarks to reclassify a groin sac and apply the repair boundary despite improved function.

concepts.displayName: Use a source-by-method pilot to select the next change
concepts.learningObjective: Separate an input-source pattern from a transfer-method pattern, then select a controlled next hypothesis while retaining outcome and burden checks.

concepts.displayName: Separate cortisol confirmation from source attribution
concepts.learningObjective: Use completed cortisol assessment to choose basal ACTH classification before attributing function to an incidental adrenal nodule.

concepts.displayName: Check the recorded phase before interpreting contractile reserve
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish completed baseline/outflow observations from an incomplete post-cluster acquisition before reporting a reserve deficit for operative assessment.

concepts.displayName: Interpret reserve separately from baseline propagation and junction relaxation
concepts.learningObjective: Use the acquired baseline, integrated post-sequence response and liquid-load behavior to choose a defensible physiological report without inferring emptying or a treatment indication.

concepts.displayName: Choose the operative plane for a symptomatic recurrent inguinal hernia
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret the archived operative anatomy and choose an offered posterior repair after prior anterior mesh surgery rather than repeat the operated plane.

concepts.displayName: Select a dynamic groin acquisition from the recorded anatomical course
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret a distal cord finding relative to the inferior epigastric vessels and select the additional acquisition that can trace its proximal origin.

concepts.displayName: Select source-directed imaging from cortisol and ACTH findings
concepts.learningObjective: Use a supported cortisol/ACTH pattern to choose adrenal imaging despite an incidental pituitary focus, rather than recall the next basal assay after suppression testing.

concepts.displayName: Positive celiac susceptibility typing
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret susceptibility typing, valid positive disease serology and a mismatched biopsy target when selecting adult celiac confirmation.

concepts.displayName: Gastric cancer with adjacent-organ invasion
concepts.learningObjective: Use organ-specific operative interfaces to distinguish indicated splenic extension from prophylactic pancreatic resection during gastric cancer surgery.

concepts.displayName: Calcification morphology and distribution
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile calcification morphology, specimen radiography and clip position before accepting a benign breast biopsy as representation of the intended target.

concepts.displayName: Phyllodes dissemination pattern
concepts.learningObjective: Use phyllodes spread biology and the actual interval targets to select representative tissue for a new distant-staging question without assuming pulmonary origin from imaging.

concepts.displayName: Perioperative respiratory acid-base trajectory
concepts.learningObjective: Detect a new respiratory CO2 contribution hidden by a concurrent alkalotic bicarbonate context and direct perioperative reassessment rather than infer recovery from pH normalization.

concepts.displayName: Rapid VKA factor replacement
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize ongoing major VKA-associated bleeding despite transient resuscitation/INR improvement and sequence immediate factor replacement alongside vitamin K.

concepts.displayName: Interpret graft-event evidence before compatibility review
concepts.learningObjective: Integrate vascular/tissue findings with actual pre-event and post-event donor/control results to choose the focus of a transplant-event review.

concepts.displayName: Select a representative node target and thyroid-directed adjunct
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret cyst-fluid adequacy and ancillary-test provenance before choosing a representative nodal target and assay.

concepts.displayName: Verify site concordance before interpreting breast imaging
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret clinical and radiology site labels before deciding whether targeted breast imaging has answered the presenting finding.

concepts.displayName: Select anorectal source control and antibiotic scope
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret residual collection and cellulitis/host findings to select drainage and the appropriate antibiotic scope.

concepts.displayName: Use graft tissue and serum specificity to direct event review
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret vascular versus cellular tissue injury and pre-event serum specificity before selecting the focus of a graft-event review.

concepts.displayName: Apply a corrected-gap report to etiologic investigation
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret blood-gas direction and albumin-adjusted versus raw gap reports before deciding whether an unmeasured-anion investigation is warranted.

concepts.displayName: Recognize nutrition risk before choosing support
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret inflammatory albumin and functional/intake trajectory before selecting structured assessment and an initial support route.

concepts.displayName: Persistent intolerance after a mucosal response
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a mucosal response from persistent fixed gastrojejunal obstruction and select the next treatment stage.

concepts.displayName: Completing a bleeding-ulcer treatment plan
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile immediate injection response with the definitive endoscopic and post-hemostasis drug components still required by a bleeding-ulcer plan.

concepts.displayName: Persistent bile drainage after a negative duct injection
concepts.learningObjective: Select anatomical localization when persistent bile drainage and an incompletely represented duct segment conflict with a negative main-duct injection.

concepts.displayName: A cure-test date after intervening medicines
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret an inadequately prepared cure test and reconcile later PPI, antibiotic and bismuth exposures when scheduling the next active-infection test.

concepts.displayName: Choosing a next fissure treatment after an interrupted course
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret an interrupted medication course and independent continence risk when selecting the next chronic-fissure treatment.

concepts.displayName: A pressure response and the next provocation
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret rapid-swallow response phase separately from outflow loading, then choose the residual symptom-matched acquisition before procedural planning.

concepts.displayName: Medication reconciliation across two procedures
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile current postoperative recovery with an imminent second fasting procedure when scheduling SGLT2 resumption.

concepts.displayName: Two missing quantities in recovery
concepts.learningObjective: Select complementary assessments of ventilation and current oxygen-carrying quantity when a saturation display and an earlier hemoglobin result are insufficient.

concepts.displayName: A corrected phosphate result during nutrition restart
concepts.learningObjective: Identify carbohydrate exposure before formula and avoid ending restart surveillance after correction of a single pre-existing phosphate abnormality.

concepts.displayName: Nutrition options for an incompletely healed incision
concepts.learningObjective: Match a wound patient's actual nutritional gap to a prescription while distinguishing a nutrient's biochemical role from a therapeutic supplementation indication.

concepts.displayName: A new bleeding phenotype and an isolated coagulation result
concepts.learningObjective: Use a new bleeding phenotype and an isolated aPTT pattern to prioritize factor-specific investigation without treating a mixing screen as a definitive gate.

concepts.displayName: A testable change during an airway intervention
concepts.learningObjective: Detect and communicate a new testable GCS component change while correctly documenting an intubation-related verbal interference.

concepts.displayName: A normal pressure supported by a new infusion
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret support-dependent recovery measurements against a patient's own agreed baseline before reinstating a temporarily modified resuscitation order.

concepts.displayName: Recipient-vessel selection for a free transfer
concepts.learningObjective: Use separate arterial and venous continuity findings to select a functional recipient pair for a proposed free transfer.

concepts.displayName: Progression after contrast leaves an IV
concepts.learningObjective: Escalate progressive local injury after contrast injection while preserving a separately documented earlier allergic-like event.

concepts.displayName: Closure planning after emergency hernia exploration
concepts.learningObjective: Use closure-related physiologic change and unresolved bowel viability to select a temporary versus definitive abdominal closure stage.

concepts.displayName: Applying a negative result in its tested population
concepts.learningObjective: Select the appropriate tested population and negative-result denominator before applying an explicitly hypothetical next-investigation rule.

concepts.displayName: A positive screen and a prespecified investigation rule
concepts.learningObjective: Use conditional test rates from unequal groups to update prior odds and apply a specified hypothetical investigation protocol.

concepts.displayName: A protocol's benefit and harm requirements
concepts.learningObjective: Compare absolute benefit and harm differences over a common horizon before applying a prespecified dual-requirement study decision.

concepts.displayName: Analyzing a pilot's changed decisions
concepts.learningObjective: Select an analysis for linked binary observations and use both discordant directions to apply a stated pilot advancement rule.

concepts.displayName: Recovery equivalence with an unresolved safety requirement
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish a met equivalence endpoint from an unresolved safety bound when choosing the next study and implementation stage.

concepts.displayName: Symptomatic medial groin defect
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile dynamic groin anatomy with functional symptoms before choosing a repair or observation plan.

concepts.displayName: Recurrent postoperative pancreatic-fluid evaluation
concepts.learningObjective: Use recurrent enzyme-rich postoperative drainage and cross-sectional findings to select duct mapping before another drainage procedure.

concepts.displayName: Nutrition during prolonged postoperative ileus
concepts.learningObjective: Plan supplemental nutrition and refeeding precautions when a malnourished postoperative patient tolerates only limited enteral delivery.

concepts.displayName: Celiac testing after gluten withdrawal
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize that negative serology or biopsy after gluten avoidance cannot settle the original celiac question and arrange a supervised diagnostic reassessment.

concepts.displayName: Celiac genetic risk versus diagnostic evidence
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret positive susceptibility typing and an isolated IgG result before choosing the appropriate initial serologic pathway.

concepts.displayName: Reassessing nutrition after ileus resolves
concepts.learningObjective: Reassess the indication for parenteral nutrition when oral and enteral delivery become adequate after prolonged ileus.

concepts.displayName: Gastric cancer with adjacent-organ invasion
concepts.learningObjective: Use organ-specific operative interfaces to distinguish indicated splenic extension from prophylactic pancreatic resection during gastric cancer surgery.

concepts.displayName: Persistent palpable breast finding after negative imaging
concepts.learningObjective: Use examination-imaging discordance to select tissue diagnosis after a correctly targeted negative study.

concepts.displayName: Grade addendum and phyllodes re-excision extent
concepts.learningObjective: Reconcile a specialist grade addendum with the current margin map before choosing the faces requiring further clearance.

concepts.displayName: New cavity finding after phyllodes surgery
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish an uncertain postoperative fluid cavity from its solid component before choosing representative tissue acquisition.

concepts.displayName: New proximal venous concern despite compressible leg veins
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret indirect proximal-obstruction findings on a technically adequate leg duplex before attributing new swelling to chronic lymphedema.

concepts.displayName: Graves medication adjustment from discordant follow-up results
concepts.learningObjective: Use thyroid-hormone and clinical trajectories rather than persistent TSH suppression to adjust antithyroid and symptom-control medicines.

concepts.displayName: Persistent thrombus versus anticoagulation failure
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish residual early thrombus from progression before adding an IVC filter or changing an effective treatment regimen.

concepts.displayName: Postoperative fatigue with normal oxygenation
concepts.learningObjective: Interpret oxygenation and red-cell measurements together to prioritize evaluation of oxygen-carrying capacity.

concepts.displayName: Perioperative respiratory acid-base trajectory
concepts.learningObjective: Detect a new respiratory CO2 contribution hidden by a concurrent alkalotic bicarbonate context and direct perioperative reassessment rather than infer recovery from pH normalization.

concepts.displayName: Early nutrition after an extensive burn
concepts.learningObjective: Reassess enteral feeding when the abdominal/perfusion trajectory deteriorates despite an earlier successful burn resuscitation.

concepts.displayName: Persistent infection after an incision is opened
concepts.learningObjective: Persistent fever and pelvic pain arise despite drainage of a different superficial pocket; imaging shows a contained accessible pelvic source. Choose the appropriate drainage route rather than extend an unrelated opening or move directly to broad abdominal surgery.

concepts.displayName: A drainage referral with two pancreatic lesions
concepts.learningObjective: Identify A as the lesion that predates pancreatitis and separate it from B's later post-necrotizing collection. Redirect the referral to characterization before planning entry into A.

concepts.displayName: Recurrent narrowing after an initial dilation
concepts.learningObjective: There is recurrent mechanical narrowing after a limited initial treatment that temporarily worked, not documented failure of a completed graded course. Continue the appropriate endoscopic strategy before treating the course as refractory and moving to stent or operation.

concepts.displayName: New bleeding after completed ulcer hemostasis
concepts.learningObjective: Separate old blood passage from a later clinically new hemorrhage after initial successful control. Choose repeat endoscopic rescue before move to arterial or operative rescue in the stabilized represented course.

concepts.displayName: A persistent fissure with limited continence reserve
concepts.learningObjective: Combine a persistent fissure with compromised sphincter reserve and the actual response to a reversible relaxation treatment. Favor a repair that preserves sphincter function rather than repeat or permanently intensify relaxation.

concepts.displayName: A changed pressure study before junction treatment
concepts.learningObjective: Identify the new relevant drug exposure between differing studies instead of accept the current pattern as a fixed primary disorder. Assess potential reversibility before add corroboration under the same exposure and commit to junction treatment.

concepts.displayName: Carbohydrate exposure before formula delivery
concepts.learningObjective: The electrolyte decline follows intravenous carbohydrate despite zero formula delivery; the delivery route does not remove the exposure. Revise the combined carbohydrate plan rather than restrict an unstarted route or substitute another carbohydrate route.

concepts.displayName: Supplemental nutrition from delivered rather than ordered intake
concepts.learningObjective: The pump record establishes actual partial delivery, while repeated rate-related interruptions limit the larger order. Reduce supplementation by the delivered contribution without treating the prescribed contribution as achieved or the bowel as fully recovered.

concepts.displayName: Protein delivery under energy and volume constraints
concepts.learningObjective: Combine food and drink contributions to distinguish a protein shortfall from an energy shortfall, while recognizing the observed meal-displacement constraint. Replace some carbohydrate contribution with protein rather than add a balanced volume or a carbohydrate module.

concepts.displayName: Repeated respiratory recurrence during opioid reversal
concepts.learningObjective: Reproducible short respiratory responses coexist with painful over-reversal after a larger peak. Choose titratable ongoing antagonism rather than repeatedly increase or reproduce bolus peaks.

concepts.displayName: Acquiring intermittent ventilation events
concepts.learningObjective: A nasal signal gap coupled to mouth position is not yet evidence that ventilation stopped; saturation on oxygen cannot decide it. Acquire the missing expiratory route at the same event time instead of substitute a between-event or slow trend value.

concepts.displayName: A normal twitch ratio after a second blocker
concepts.learningObjective: The first twitch recovered after the original reversal, then fell after a different blocker without marked fade. Do not apply rocuronium reversal to that new depolarizing-agent pattern.

concepts.displayName: Anticoagulant selection during changing renal function
concepts.learningObjective: Recognize proximal thrombosis and, separately, that a moving creatinine cannot be treated as stable chronic kidney function before a pending procedure. Select a titratable initial inpatient agent instead of carry a routine outpatient regimen into that unstable transition.

concepts.displayName: Two heparin orders with different purposes
concepts.learningObjective: The therapeutic order derives from an AF interruption, while the lower-intensity order derives from the cancer operation; a low INR does not merge those indications. Remove the unnecessary bridge without inadvertently cancelling surgical prophylaxis.

concepts.displayName: A motor change hidden by a global score
concepts.learningObjective: The best motor score can remain unchanged while one arm loses command following; unchanged sedation and the contralateral response matter. Escalate structural neurologic assessment rather than use the global score, drug exposure or small gas variation to dismiss the change.

concepts.displayName: A current request during a temporary perioperative directive
concepts.learningObjective: Infer decision-specific understanding from the actual explanation and consistency instead of automatically defer to a surrogate or prior order. Conduct current reconsideration with the patient and document intervention limits before the old endpoint.

concepts.displayName: A recipient bed that changes before coverage
concepts.learningObjective: Distinguish the original avascular cortical surface from the currently prepared tissue-covered surface and assess the remaining structural requirements. Choose coverage based on the current recipient bed rather than automatically import a flap because the first debridement exposed bone.

concepts.displayName: A changed free-flap recovery pattern
concepts.learningObjective: Infer an outflow concern from several interval observations rather than assume a sound arterial signal certifies the circulation. concepts.displayName: Outcome-dependent wound coding in an infection audit

concepts.displayName: An urgent limb change during contrast administration

decisionNodes.stem: How should you manage this patient's tumor initially?

answerChoices.label: Immediate wide excision solely to obtain a large negative margin
Routine cytotoxic chemotherapy for every confirmed desmoid
Incision and drainage of the solid tumor

decisionNodes.explanation: For newly diagnosed desmoid disease without persistent progression, critical-site threat, obstruction, or meaningful functional decline, specialist active surveillance is an appropriate initial strategy. Routine upfront surgery or cytotoxic therapy is not required for every confirmed desmoid.

decisionNodes.stem: At a later specialist follow-up, serial assessment shows persistent enlargement with increasing pain and impaired mobility. The abdominal-wall tumor remains resectable with acceptably low expected morbidity. What is the most appropriate next plan?

answerChoices.label: Continue observation despite progressive functional loss
Radical excision regardless of avoidable functional morbidity

decisionNodes.explanation: Persistent progression with meaningful pain or functional loss warrants renewed multidisciplinary treatment planning. For resectable abdominal-wall disease with acceptably low expected morbidity, function-preserving surgery may be proposed; the same rule does not make surgery universal for every location.

decisionNodes.stem:
Which cause of thyrotoxicosis most likely explains this patient's
findings?
decisionNodes.explanation:
The diffuse thyroid enlargement with bilateral proptosis
supports Graves disease in the setting of symptoms compatible with
thyroid-hormone excess. Painful subacute thyroiditis and nodular causes are
alternative causes of thyrotoxicosis, but do not describe this full pattern.

decisionNodes.stem: Which tissue-diagnosis plan best protects the patient's later definitive treatment options?
decisionNodes.explanation: Suspicious MRI should prompt referral to an experienced sarcoma team before biopsy. A planned image-guided core biopsy can obtain tissue while placing the biopsy tract where it can be managed within a future surgical approach; MRI suspicion alone is not sarcoma confirmation.

decisionNodes.stem: Which Act-step decision fits the authorized celiac pathway pilot when its symptom aim is met and the balancing measure does not worsen?

answerChoices.label: Adopt locally and plan the next test
answerChoices.rationale: The test met its aim without worsening balance in the tested setting. Local adoption uses that learning while a next linked test investigates the next step.

answerChoices.label: Spread the change and monitor other clinics
answerChoices.rationale: The results apply to the local test. Spreading immediately to other clinics goes beyond that scope instead of testing the next setting.

answerChoices.label: Repeat the same pilot before making any change
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied favorable aim and balancing findings support local action. Repeating the identical pilot without acting does not use the stated learning.

answerChoices.label: Adapt the pathway before another local test
answerChoices.rationale: The findings identify no feature requiring revision before local adoption. Adaptation needs a reason in the learning, rather than a change for its own sake.

decisionNodes.explanation: Adopt the successful pathway locally and plan the next linked test. The favorable aim and balancing findings apply to the tested setting, not an untested wider rollout.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: The Act step turns learning into a decision and a next test. This pathway version met its aim without worsening the balancing measure, supporting local adoption and a linked next cycle. Keep the scope of action tied to the scope of the evidence: a successful small test does not automatically establish performance at every clinic.

decisionNodes.stem: Which Act-step decision fits the authorized venous-ulcer device pilot when healing is faster but application rework doubles?

answerChoices.label: Adapt device use and retest locally
answerChoices.rationale: Healing improved but rework doubled. Revise device use to address that burden and use the next test to study the adapted version.

answerChoices.label: Adopt device use and monitor application rework
answerChoices.rationale: Adopting this version unchanged accepts the documented worsening of rework. The balancing finding calls for adaptation before adoption.

answerChoices.label: Abandon device use and test another local idea
answerChoices.rationale: The target improvement supports retaining and adapting the idea. The supplied findings do not require discarding it instead of addressing the added burden.

answerChoices.label: Repeat device use without revising the process
answerChoices.rationale: Repeating the same device unchanged does not respond to the increased rework already observed. The next cycle should use that learning.

decisionNodes.explanation: Adapt device use to address increased rework, then retest. The improved healing target supports keeping the idea, while the worsened balancing measure argues against adopting this version unchanged.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Improvement needs both the intended result and a check for shifted burden. This device shortened wound-closure time but doubled rework, so adapt its use and retest rather than adopting the current version unchanged. The Act step can preserve a promising idea while changing the part that caused trouble. Learning should change the next cycle.

decisionNodes.stem: What should the team tell {patientName} about the wrong-chart error that materially affected the tissue-biopsy discussion, despite no demonstrated injury?

answerChoices.label: Explain the material error and its correction
answerChoices.rationale: The wrong-chart recommendation materially affected care information. Explain that mistake and its correction even though it was intercepted without demonstrated injury.

answerChoices.label: Discuss the corrected recommendation and defer the error
answerChoices.rationale: Silently giving a corrected recommendation omits the material error that changed the earlier discussion. Absence of injury is not a blanket reason to leave it unexplained.

answerChoices.label: Use the internal safety report as the disclosure response
answerChoices.rationale: Internal reporting and patient disclosure serve different parts of the response. Filing a report does not tell the patient about the material mistake and correction.

answerChoices.label: Wait for an injury assessment before discussing the mistake
answerChoices.rationale: The supplied error materially affected the care discussion. Waiting to demonstrate injury treats harm as a blanket disclosure requirement that the existing claim does not impose.

decisionNodes.explanation: Explain the material wrong-chart error and its correction. An internal report or silent replacement of the recommendation does not substitute for candid disclosure merely because no injury is demonstrated.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: An error can materially affect a care discussion even when it is intercepted before treatment and no injury is demonstrated. That absence of harm is not a blanket reason to conceal it. Explain the material mistake and correction honestly. Consider what changed the patient's care information, rather than using injury alone as the disclosure test.

AST PTLD and EBV guideline
Comprehensive review of PTLD after solid organ transplantation

decisionNodes.stem: What should research consent explain when {patientName} expects personally selected treatment in a desmoid-agent trial whose protocol uses random allocation?

answerChoices.label: Assignment is random and benefit is uncertain
answerChoices.rationale: The approved protocol assigns randomly and guarantees no better arm. Clarifying both points corrects the expectation of personally selected treatment with assured benefit.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is clinical and benefit is individualized
answerChoices.rationale: The protocol does not use individualized clinical selection. This wording preserves the patient's mistaken expectation instead of explaining random allocation and uncertain benefit.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is random and benefit is established
answerChoices.rationale: Random assignment is correct, but established benefit is not. No arm is guaranteed better in the supplied protocol.

answerChoices.label: Assignment is chosen and benefit is uncertain
answerChoices.rationale: Uncertainty about benefit is correct, but assignment is not chosen by the surgeon or participant. The protocol uses random allocation.

decisionNodes.explanation: Explain that assignment is random and benefit uncertain. The protocol does not let the surgeon select a personally best arm or guarantee that an arm will be better.
decisionNodes.teachingPoint: Research consent needs a clear account of allocation and uncertainty. This protocol assigns arms randomly; the surgeon does not choose a personally best arm, and benefit is not guaranteed. Remember to distinguish a research protocol from individually selected treatment. Understanding assignment helps the patient choose whether to join, not a detail for after enrollment.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial clinical management plan best fits {patientName}'s newly diagnosed, stable, minimally symptomatic abdominal-wall desmoid tumor without threatened function or a critical structure?

answerChoices.label: Specialist active surveillance with follow-up

answerChoices.label: Immediate wide excision with margin assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Immediate wide excision is not required for every newly diagnosed stable desmoid. The supplied findings support specialist surveillance first.

answerChoices.label: Cytotoxic chemotherapy with specialist follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: Routine upfront cytotoxic therapy is not required for the selected stable, noncritical disease described here.

answerChoices.label: Incision and drainage with wound follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: The biopsy-confirmed desmoid is a solid tumor, rather than a collection for incision and drainage.

decisionNodes.explanation: Specialist active surveillance fits this newly diagnosed, stable desmoid without critical threat or functional decline. The existing objective does not require immediate surgery or cytotoxic therapy.

decisionNodes.stem: What is the best response to an unexplained ART omission when oral therapy is feasible?

answerChoices.label: Reconcile and continue the prescribed ART
Restart the first listed ART component
Restart the ward single-drug ART substitute

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Reconcile and continue the prescribed ART.” An omission calls for coordinated medication reconciliation, not a routine postoperative hold. The unexplained hold should be reconciled when administration is feasible. A partial regimen is not coordinated ART continuation. Uncoordinated partial substitution does not restore the prescribed regimen.
sourceLabels: Perioperative Care in Adults With HIV

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The reconciled medication list includes cobicistat. The anesthesia team now asks about its interaction with midazolam.
decisionNodes.stem: Which mechanism explains the midazolam interaction with cobicistat?
decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Inhibition of CYP3A-mediated metabolism.” Reduced metabolism can increase midazolam exposure and prolong sedation. The booster warning concerns metabolic inhibition rather than increased renal elimination. Reduced absorption does not explain increased exposure from CYP3A inhibition. The relevant booster effect inhibits rather than induces midazolam metabolism.

decisionNodes.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes monitored IV from oral midazolam with boosted ART?

answerChoices.label: IV use needs reviewed dosing and monitoring
IV use can proceed under the unchanged dose plan
Oral substitution is preferable to monitored IV use
IV use calls for withholding the ART regimen

decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “IV use needs reviewed dosing and monitoring.” Parenteral midazolam may be considered with appropriate monitoring and individualized dose review; oral restrictions should not be copied wholesale. Changing route does not erase the need to assess increased exposure. The oral route has the contraindication; monitored parenteral use is assessed differently. ART interruption is not the default solution to an interaction requiring sedation planning.

decisionNodes.stem: Which drug in this completed anesthetic record is specifically complexed by sugammadex?
decisionNodes.explanation: The correct answer is “Rocuronium.” Sugammadex selectively binds this steroidal neuromuscular blocker. Sugammadex binding selectivity for rocuronium and vecuronium should not be extrapolated to this blocker. This is not one of the blockers selectively complexed by sugammadex. The labeled rocuronium and vecuronium selectivity does not establish reversal of this blocker.

answerChoices.rationale: The clot-filled tender lump lies beneath external anal skin, which identifies the external thrombosis pattern.

answerChoices.rationale: The supplied lesion is under external skin, without protruding mucosal tissue from the anal canal.

decisionNodes.stem: Which initial evaluation step should clarify William Scott's undocumented penicillin-allergy label before ambulatory surgery?

answerChoices.label: Obtain a detailed drug-reaction history
answerChoices.rationale: Clarify the original drug, symptoms, timing, severity and later exposures before choosing an evaluation pathway or changing the record.

answerChoices.label: Schedule penicillin skin prick testing
answerChoices.rationale: Testing should follow history and risk assessment; an incompletely characterized label does not by itself select this pathway.

answerChoices.label: Schedule a supervised oral drug challenge
answerChoices.rationale: A supervised challenge can be appropriate for selected patients, but this incomplete history has not yet established suitability.

answerChoices.label: Remove penicillin from the allergy record
answerChoices.rationale: The record should not be changed solely because the reaction is unclear. First characterize the history and assess the appropriate evaluation.

  acceptanceId: string; caseId: string; nodeId: string; questionVariantId: string; conceptId: string;
  sourceView: string; decision: string;
}

  replaces: string;
  with: string;
